item.title: [Rising Apple] 1 dream target, 1 realistic target, 1 mistake NY Mets could make in Tarik Skubal backup plans

item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets will surely be in on two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal in free agency. But it won't be easy to land Skubal, who could draw the richest contract for a starting pitcher in MLB history.
The Mets must add starting pitching this offseason, whether they sign Skubal or not. So, if they miss out on Skubal, let's take a look at one dream target, one realistic target and one mistake the Mets could make as Plan B.
The Tarik Skubal backup plans for the Mets
The Dream Target
If the Mets can't lure Skubal to Queens, right-handed starter Michael King would be a dream target for their pivot plan. King has an opt-out in his deal this offseason that he could exercise to test the open market. King is coming off a strong season with the San Diego Padres, where he went 12-10 with a 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP, 127 ERA+. 4.13 FIP, 159 strikeouts and a 4.3 bWAR in 32 starts and 185 innings. He also came up clutch in the postseason with a 0.64 ERA in three appearances (two starts).
King is a proven arm, who has pitched on the big stage and performed well. He began his career with the Yankees, where he spent his first five seasons in the big leagues. Should the Mets not sign Skubal, King would be a dream move and positive veteran presence to add to a rotation that features a trio of youngsters: Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.
The realistic target
Why does it feel like a reunion could be brewing between Clay Holmes and the Mets? Holmes, a former All-Star reliever and closer, signed a three-year, $38 million deal to become a starter with the Mets ahead of the 2025 season. The Mets got the most out of Holmes during his time in Queens, posting a 16-12 record and 3.26 ERA in 42 appearances and 40 starts. Holmes had a 2.39 ERA in nine starts to begin the 2026 season with the Mets, but broke his leg in a May outing after getting hit by a comebacker.
The Mets dealt Holmes to the Chicago Cubs at the trade deadline, and he proceeded to produce a 4.25 ERA in his final nine starts. Holmes is known for being a ground ball pitcher, so the Mets should focus on improving their infield defense if they bring him back. It feels like re-signing Holmes is a realistic move for the Mets given his success with the team as a starter. Holmes is expected to opt-out of his deal this offseason.
The mistake
Trading for Tampa Bay Rays ace Drew Rasmussen seems like a good move given recency bias, but it would ultimately be a mistake. Rasmussen has a $20 million club option for 2027 and will be a free agent after next season if it is exercised. The Mets would have to give up multiple prospects to acquire one season of his services, and they just made a similar deal for Freddy Peralta, which didn't work out.
Rasmussen turns 32-years-old next season, has had multiple elbow surgeries and has three good campaigns under his belt across a seven-year career. It would be a mistake for the Mets to give up assets to acquire just one season of Rasmussen via trade. The Mets would be unlikely to re-sign him to a long-term deal following 2027 given his age and injury history.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Scott Boras Lays Out Tarik Skubal Free Agency Outlook Ahead of Dodgers Talks
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is entering free agency, and his renowned baseball agent, Scott Boras, discussed his marquee client’s free-agent status.
Scott Boras’ reputation
Boras is known for being an aggressive negotiator who typically refuses contract extensions throughout a player’s career, letting them enter free agency and letting the free market decide their ultimate value.
When it comes to getting the best possible deal for his clients, especially the top ones, no one in baseball has a more stellar reputation.
However, while that often benefits his clients, teams can struggle to lock down their players when Boras is in the mix.
With Skubal, Boras is in a position to do what he does best: explore the market, try to spark a bidding war, and land a massive deal that should break records.
How he views Skubal’s market
Skubal’s status as one of the best pitchers alive makes a sales pitch unnecessary. Boras, when speaking to The Athletic’s Andy McCullough, made an interesting statement that relays how he views his client.
“Last time around, everybody talked about Skuby Doo. It’s kind of like, with Skubal now, it’s Skuby Done. He’s proven it at all levels, in different markets, in different environments,” Boras told The Athletic.
How long will it take for Skubal to sign?
Boras is typically not shy about waiting for the best possible deal and letting some teams panic about getting a deal done.
With a lockout coming on December 1st, Boras thinks teams will be highly motivated to secure players before a new set of rules comes into place.
“For many teams, I can make an argument it’s clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after,” Boras told The Athletic.
“Because they have more freedom to do what they’re going to do. They can react later. Now they can get the talent. They can get what they want.”
The Dodgers, who will be talking to Boras, and the rest of the league, will need to make their pitches and offers quickly and be ready to negotiate fast, because the best player in free agency may not be available for long.

item.content:encoded:
In an offseason of many transitions for the Los Angeles Dodgers, one decision looms among the largest.
When the two-time defending champions traded for two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, there was a certain amount of risk attacked to it.
The risk was not necessarily in terms of play as he attained a 2.61 ERA in his 10 regular season starts as a Dodger, but with the fact that Skubal would become a free agent when the season ended.
The season ended far earlier than anyone around the organization would have wanted, and now Skubal is entering free agency as by far the best player available. The team that ends up succesfully courting the soon-to-be 30-year-old Skubal, however, is expected to potentially spend close to $500 million to lock him down.
President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman was asked about Skubal at the team's end-of-season press conference, and praised him for his quick transition to a new team.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said. “The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time.”
As for Skubal's postseason play, as expected, he excelled.
In two October starts (11 innings), he had a 2.45 ERA, striking out 14 and walking four.
Now Friedman has an opportunity to ensure that those weren't the final two starts of Skubal's Dodgers tenure.
In terms of Skubal's free agency, Friedman avoided much discourse, instead saying Skubal will make a business decision at the end of the day, and all the organization can do is have discussions with his agent, Scott Boras.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent. And for us, it’s [to] continue to talk to Scott," Friedman said. "But he and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
The hope for LA is that Skubal's talents can be long appreciated at Dodger Stadium, and that he doesn't join the unfortunate list of trade deadline acquisitions who left the following offseason.
Though some worked out more than others, players like Yu Darvish, Manny Machado, Max Scherzer and most recently Jack Flaherty (who also came from the Detroit Tigers) are each a part of a list that Dodgers fans will hope to not see Skubal on.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal is the top free agent on the market. On top of that he is a left-handed ace that should be the Opening Day starter for any team in the league not named the Los Angeles Dodgers, Atlanta Braves, Milwaukee Brewers or Pittsburgh Pirates… and even those teams would strongly consider putting Skubal on the mound in Game 1 of the 2027 season.
The San Diego Padres have been rumored as a possible landing spot for the lefty in at least a few publications, and the argument for the move is that it would echo the commitment new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones made in press conferences and in their end-of-season letter to season ticket holders. The Padres are in need of pitching this offseason and a move to land Skubal would show the Padres fans and MLB the new owners mean what they say.
The question all San Diego fans have to ask themselves is whether or not Skubal is worth the huge payday he is expected to get. Padres fans know all too well how volatile a pitcher can be. Joe Musgrove missed the majority of two seasons with an elbow injury, Nick Pivetta missed most of the 2026 season with an arm injury and Yu Darvish never touched the mound this season as a result of an arm injury. San Diego ace and likely soon-to-be free agent Michael King missed a chunk of the 2025 season because he "slept wrong" and injured a nerve in his shoulder/neck.
Should the Padres want to spread their money around, whatever amount that might be, they may be better served. King is likely to opt-out of his contract and enter free agency. Reliever Adrian Morejon is a free agent and Ty France who many believe is the 2026 team MVP for the Padres is also a free agent. If Skubal wants $400 million-plus, it may be too rich for one player on a team that needs several players in the rotation and in the starting lineup.
San Diego could have a rotation of Pivetta, if the Padres pick up his option, Musgrove and Randy Vasquez. Others who could make a push for the spot like JP Sears are also on the roster, but unlikely to find what is needed to be in the San Diego rotation to start the season. Musgrove is still an unknown in terms of what he can provide and Darvish COULD return, but he could also just as easily retire depending on how he feels once he gets back to throwing competitive pitches off the mound.
This is an important offseason for the new ownership and as flashy as a Skubal signing might be, it may not be the most beneficial move for the team.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy is still playing at an All-Star level, but how much longer can he keep it up?
After narrowly defeating the Toronto Blue Jays in the 2025 World Series, the Dodgers knew they were on the cusp of history. They went and added to their already star-studded roster by acquiring Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz in the offseason before trading for back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal at the MLB Trade Deadline.
But the Dodgers, with the most expensive roster and all the championship pedigree in the world, could not get past the young and hungry Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers got their revenge on Los Angeles for being swept in the 2025 National League Championship Series by returning the favor on the same stage this season.
The thing about the Dodgers is that they were not the powerhouse we were used to seeing throughout the season, and their struggles and injuries eventually culminated in their demise.
Sure, they won 100 games, but the cracks in an aging roster were evident. Now it begs the question of how much time some of the veteran leaders of this team have left to compete for a title.
One such player who is closer to the end of his career than the beginning is third baseman Max Muncy. Let's evaluate the type of season he had.
Strong and stable
The 36-year-old appeared in 149 regular season games and did not serve a stint on the Injured List. Over the course of those games, Muncy took 488 at-bats and posted a .252 batting average, a .348 on-base percentage, a .490 slugging percentage and an .838 OPS with 29 home runs, the most he has hit since the 2023 season.
For his efforts, Muncy earned his third All-Star selection.
For a little while during the playoffs, it seemed as if Muncy would continue to be a catalyst for his team's offense. In four games against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Division Series, Muncy hit three home runs.
However, like the rest of the Dodgers' offense, Muncy lost steam against the Brewers and went just 2-for-12 at the plate while striking out six times.
It is good that Muncy was healthy in 2026, and Los Angeles certainly needed it. But it does not change the fact that he has passed his prime, and eventually a decision will have to be made by both him and the team about where things stand.
In 2027, Muncy is on the payroll for $10.7 million. In 2028, which will be his age-37 season, the Dodgers have a club option. At that point, serious discussions will need to be had.
Muncy has dealt with injuries in the past but has otherwise stayed relatively healthy throughout his career. If he keeps his production up, there is a chance that he could remain in Dodger blue well into his late 30s.
Whatever the future brings, there is no doubting how important he has been to the franchise.

item.title: [FanSided] The latest Tarik Skubal free agency news should leave baseball fans extremely concerned
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Even with the growing possibility of baseball’s longest work stoppage since the 1994-95 players’ strike, there’s no doubt Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal is about to earn big money. Pitchers like Skubal, who owns two Cy Young Awards and a .247 ERA since the start of 2023, aren’t typically available in their prime. item.content:encoded:
Even with the growing possibility of baseball’s longest work stoppage since the 1994-95 players’ strike, there’s no doubt Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal is about to earn big money.
Pitchers like Skubal, who owns two Cy Young Awards and a .247 ERA since the start of 2023, aren’t typically available in their prime. What team wouldn’t want to add a perennial All-Star who will pitch all of next season — assuming there is a 2027 season — at 30 years old? (Outside of the Rockies, Rays, and Guardians, of course.)
Owners want a salary cap and competitive balance, but the majority also want championships. The Athletic’s Andy McCullough spoke with Scott Boras, who represents Skubal, and multiple executives, all of whom agreed Skubal should still cash in; an unnamed executive told McCullough they believe Skubal could sign a 10-year, $400 million contract.
“Last time around, everybody talked about Skuby Doo,” Boras told McCullough. “It’s kind of like, with Skubal now, it’s Skuby Done. He’s proven it at all levels, in different markets, in different environments.”
Not even a lockout will stop ace Tarik Skubal from getting paid
In essence, Major League Baseball and its owners want to cut spending where possible. Look no further than the proposed contract limits, which would cap a free agent’s next deal at five years and $202 million. In that theoretical situation, Skubal also would have had the opportunity to re-sign with the Dodgers for no more than six years and $265 million.
On the one hand, we’re personally against teams handing out 10-year deals because they never age well. The best-case scenario is winning a championship in a player’s prime, as the Dodgers did with Shohei Ohtani (10 years, $700 million) and Yoshinobu Yamamoto (12 years, $325 million) the last two years. Otherwise, you wind up watching the player become dead weight on an inescapable contract, as the Padres are learning with Xander Bogaerts.
But that doesn’t mean we’re against players earning those deals. Why would anyone turn down a contract worth that much money, especially with deferrals? Just because we disagree with a team’s reasoning doesn’t mean Skubal or Ohtani didn’t deserve the opportunity.
Plenty of baseball fans, especially those in smaller markets, might disagree. They want a world where the Brewers, Guardians, and Rays compete for championships every year, and the Dodgers and Yankees aren’t guaranteed a World Series appearance. Never mind that the Yankees have had only one pennant since the start of 2010.
But if annual heavy spenders like the Yankees, Dodgers, and Mets want Skubal, they may make their move ahead of the lockout. We imagine it all depends on how quickly the dominant lefty wants to sign, though we’d personally advise him to do so ASAP.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Make Tarik Skubal Interest Clear Ahead of Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal will reach free agency the day after the World Series, and the incumbent team will be among the first to call. The Dodgers acquired Skubal in August, right at the trade deadline, hoping he would be the final piece to a three-peat, but a struggling offense kept them from reaching that goal. Despite still reeling from the disappointment, Dodgers President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman was not shy about celebrating how well Skubal assimilat
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal will reach free agency the day after the World Series, and the incumbent team will be among the first to call.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal in August, right at the trade deadline, hoping he would be the final piece to a three-peat, but a struggling offense kept them from reaching that goal.
Despite still reeling from the disappointment, Dodgers President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman was not shy about celebrating how well Skubal assimilated into the Dodgers and their mission.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said to Dodgers Nation and the media. “You have set routines, and you have to make those adjustments.
“The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time. We have a tremendous amount of respect for him on and off the field.”
The lefty posted a 2.45 ERA in two postseason starts for the Dodgers, down from 2.61 in his regular-season starts.
However, he may have made his last start with the Dodgers, now that superagent Scott Boras controls his future.
Friedman clearly understands what lies ahead, and while he made no promises, he made it clear he’ll talk with Boras.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent. And for us, it’s (to) continue to talk to Scott (Boras),” Friedman told the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“But he and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
The Dodgers will be in the market for Skubal, and they have the financial means to stay in it for a while, possibly even to the end, and keep their super rotation together.

item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal is (almost) officially a free agent, and he's keeping his cards close to his chest. After the Dodgers' exit from the postseason, he declined to comment on his thoughts about going back to LA. Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said that they'll continue having conversations with Skubal and Scott Boras, but it's ultimately up to Skubal to make the best decision for himself and his family.
This is just the done thing when a player becomes a free agent. The odds that he goes back to to LA are massive, even as a slate of other teams may be preparing to make their own pitches.
The Tigers have been included on almost every "teams to watch" list when it comes to the Skubal sweepstakes, but fans know better than to get our hopes up about that. With the amount of money coming off the payroll this offseason, it might not be impossible, but the odds are incredibly slim.
There's an elephant in the room, of course: baseball is barreling toward a lockout. The challenge for this crop of free agents will be signing before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 without sacrificing their own value in the rush.
If anyone is equipped to do that for Skubal, it's Boras. He said broadly, "For many teams, I can make an argument it's clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after..."
Sounds like we won't have to wait too long to find out where Skubal will end up.
Scott Boras hints it won't take long for Tarik Skubal to sign a new contract ahead of an MLB lockout
Although a salary cap almost certainly isn't going to fly in any world, as much as the owners and a large contingent of baseball fans want it to, players who wait until the smoke clears to sign are at a distinct disadvantage. There will be little runway for those without new homes to negotiate and sign before the start of what figures to be an abbreviated season.
It's hard to see how players might have more leverage before and after a lockout, but if anyone can make the argument, it's Boras. The teams that want Skubal are going to have to come out swinging immediately, and it's hard to envision a world in which the Tigers are one of them.
At least we probably won't be kept in suspense for very long. Anyone who's seriously interested in Skubal is going to have to come out swinging and start the bidding high. The Tigers aren't in a position to compete with the likes of the Dodgers are Mets, nor have they given any indication that they want to be.

item.title: [New York Post] Why Dodgers remain coy on potential Tarik Skubal re-signing: ‘Wish him nothing but the best’
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: When it comes to top free agents, the Dodgers rarely tip their hand. At the outset of Tarik Skubal’s free agency this offseason, that remained the case once again. During an end-of-season press conference on Wednesday, less than a week removed from the team’s sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman carefully sidestepped a question about Skubal, saying a lot of words that offered no substantive indica
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to top free agents, the Dodgers rarely tip their hand.
At the outset of Tarik Skubal’s free agency this offseason, that remained the case once again.
During an end-of-season press conference on Wednesday, less than a week removed from the team’s sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman carefully sidestepped a question about Skubal, saying a lot of words that offered no substantive indication of the club’s urgency level to potentially re-sign him.
Friedman started by praising the two-time Cy Young Award-winning left-hander, whom the Dodgers acquired in a blockbuster trade deadline deal with the Detroit Tigers in August.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said. “You have set routines, and you have to make those adjustments.”
The longtime top executive then complimented the way Skubal acclimated to his new surroundings, and the impact he made even in a year the Dodgers fell short of a World Series three-peat.
“The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time,” Friedman said. “We have a tremendous amount of respect for him on and off the field.”
What Friedman didn’t do, however, was say that the Dodgers would be all-in on Skubal this winter, or that they would do whatever it takes to lock him up in a free agency process that is expected to end with the soon-to-be 30-year-old breaking Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s record guarantee of $325 million for a pitcher.
That wasn’t unexpected, of course.
Even in the run-up to this year’s deadline, the Dodgers publicly downplayed how aggressive they would be for the superstar ace.
Still, by playing it coy Wednesday, Friedman allowed a vacuum of speculation to develop about exactly where the Dodgers will stand in the Skubal sweepstakes.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent,” Friedman said, acknowledging only that the club will have conversations with Skubal’s agent, Scott Boras, going into the winter. “He and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
Granted, it’s still extremely early in the offseason. And as the Dodgers have shown the last couple winters, they can never be counted out for a top free-agent target (remember when they were supposedly not going to break the bank for Kyle Tucker?).
At this point, however, there have been questions from some corners of the industry about the Dodgers’ willingness to give Skubal the lengthy, lucrative contract he will be seeking.
The team already has ample future financial commitments tied up to Yamamoto, Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts and others. Even without Skubal, they will have one of the majors’ best rotations next year, assuming Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki continue to develop, and Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow can avoid the injury problems that have plagued them the past few years.
Much could depend on the league’s looming CBA negotiations, which might result in a salary cap –– or some other drastic changes to the sport’s economic structure –– following a lockout all but certain to commence on Dec. 1.
It’s unclear if Skubal will try to sign a new contract before then; with the Mets, Cubs, Angels and Yankees all seen as potential suitors, among others.
It’s also unclear how the Dodgers’ approach to long-term payroll might change depending on what the new CBA entails.
That’s why, for now, the club will remain the ultimate wild card in his free-agency process.
They have the resources to swing a record-breaking deal if they want. They have a track record of getting aggressive for players they feel swing their World Series chances. But if they are planning an all-out press to re-sign Skubal, they aren’t tipping their hand yet.
“We’re still wrapping our arms around our off-season plan and strategy and timing of things,” Friedman said.
His cards, once again, were staying glued to his chest.

item.title: [Bolavip US] Dodgers GM reaffirms commitment to Kyle Tucker, Edwin Diaz heading into next season
item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: Two of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ premier additions last offseason, Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz, endured turbulent 2026 regular seasons. Despite those struggles, General Manager Brandon Gomes expressed strong confidence in both players looking ahead to 2027. “So much of that was betting on the true talent of those guys and while the regular season did not go the way anyone expected, their contributions in the postseason were massive,” Gomes said. “Really looking forward to next year for those guys.
item.content:encoded:
Two of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ premier additions last offseason, Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz, endured turbulent 2026 regular seasons. Despite those struggles, General Manager Brandon Gomes expressed strong confidence in both players looking ahead to 2027.
“So much of that was betting on the true talent of those guys and while the regular season did not go the way anyone expected, their contributions in the postseason were massive,” Gomes said. “Really looking forward to next year for those guys.”
With both players anchored in Los Angeles—alongside ace Tarik Skubal, whose long-term future remains a key storyline—the Dodgers aim to rebound in 2027 and recapture World Series glory following their back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025.
Another major focal point in Los Angeles was the late-season performance of Shohei Ohtani. The Japanese superstar struggled to find his dominant form in October after racing back from an injury sustained in the closing weeks of the regular season.
Edwin Diaz #3 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts.
Diaz and Tucker’s performances in the 2026 MLB season
Across 21 regular-season appearances, Diaz struggled to an inflated 8.68 ERA and a 1.98 WHIP over 18.2 innings, battling command issues and giving up crucial late-game hits. While he managed to secure seven saves, he frequently pitched through traffic on the basepaths. However, the fiery reliever found redemption in October, delivering multiple scoreless relief outings to stabilize the back end of the bullpen when the Dodgers needed it most.
For Tucker, the 2026 campaign was marked by flashes of production bookending a lengthy middle-of-the-season injury absence. Tucker finished his abbreviated regular season hitting .239 with 70 hits, seven home runs, and 44 RBIs across 80 games.
His refined plate discipline and smooth left-handed swing remained vital assets, allowing him to maintain a solid on-base percentage and deliver timely hits with runners in scoring position.
Key takeaways
- Brandon Gomes praised Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz’s postseason contributions despite regular-season struggles.
- Edwin Diaz recorded a 8.68 ERA and a 1.98 WHIP across 21 regular-season appearances.
- Kyle Tucker posted a .239 batting average with 7 home runs and 44 RBIs.

item.dc:creator: Jake Mintz
