item.content:encoded:
A LOS Angeles Dodgers star has sent a message to the fans after the World Series hero entered free agency.
The Dodgers were denied a chance at three consecutive World Series titles this year after they were brutally swept in the NLCS.
In a somewhat shocking affair, the Milwaukee Brewers got out the broom and brushed aside a $340 million payroll outfit inside three.
Just hours after the Brewers returned to the World Series for the first time since 1982, Dodgers hero Miguel Rojas announced his retirement.
And now it seems like more core members of the Dodgers’ back-to-back crew will be on their way out of LA.
The Dodgers have a number of stars hitting free agency, with star reliever Alex Vesia one of them.
READ MORE ON BASEBALL
After superstar pitcher Tarik Skubal, there is no player whose departure will hit harder than Vesia’s.
He has been an integral part of the Dodgers bullpen since 2021, but he has no idea whether he will be returning for the 2027 MLB season.
Vesia, 30, took to his Instagram to share a message with the Dodgers fanbase after their troubling defeat to the Brewers.
“By far the hardest year of my career. It’s hard to put into words what this season was like,” Vesia wrote in his Instagram caption.
How to watch the MLB post-season
MLB has new national TV deals for 2026-28 with ESPN, NBCUniversal, and Netflix. Several elements of MLB's national broadcast rights have not changed, including Fox, Warner Bros., and Apple Inc. deals for national coverage.
NBC returned to regular broadcast MLB coverage for the first time in 25 years. And Netflix made yet another significant move into live event coverage.
NBC: Sunday Night Baseball (moving from ESPN), Sunday Leadoff Games, whole Wild Card series, Labor Day primetime games and Opening Day primetime games
Netflix: Opening Night exclusive game, T-Mobile Home Run Derby, MLB at Field of Dreams Game (Beginning 2026), World Baseball Classic in Japan
ESPN: National midweek game package (30 games), secured the rights to sell and distribute MLB.TV into the ESPN app

“Personal battles with confidence, expectations and highs and lows mentally.
“I can’t thank my teammates enough for picking me up on down days and dealing with my crazy ass on my high ones.
“I don’t know what the future holds, but I do want to say thank you to Dodger Nation for showing me so much love over the past 6 years, especially this year. I’m just a man on a mission!”
Following his 2024 World Series heroics, allowing only one hit and one walk while striking out two in 2 and two-third scoreless innings, the next season was a tremendously tough one for Vesia.
He and his wife Kayla lost their newborn daughter right before the 2025 World Series in October that year, which he sat out of as a result.
Showing how much he meant to the team, Vesia’s teammates paid tribute by having his number 51 stitched into their caps for the World Series.
Despite his tough off-the-field situation, the 30-year-old bounced back with a 2.64 ERA across 72 appearances this season.
Vesia would certainly be missed by all of Dodgers nation should he be allowed to walk this offseason.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tigers Can Have Tarik Skubal Back at a Record Price
item.dc:creator: Glenn Kaplan
item.description: The Detroit Tigers traded starting pitcher Tarik Skubal to the Los Angeles Dodgers for outfielder Zyhir Hope and right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith on Aug. 1, a day and a half before the 2026 MLB trade deadline. Skubal was playing out the final year of his contract on a $32 million arbitration salary, and the Tigers wanted to get something back rather than watch him leave for nothing. The question now is what kind of pay day he gets on the open market. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year, $325 mi
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Tigers traded starting pitcher Tarik Skubal to the Los Angeles Dodgers for outfielder Zyhir Hope and right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith on Aug. 1, a day and a half before the 2026 MLB trade deadline. Skubal was playing out the final year of his contract on a $32 million arbitration salary, and the Tigers wanted to get something back rather than watch him leave for nothing.
The question now is what kind of pay day he gets on the open market. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers is still the largest guarantee ever handed to a pitcher, and the projections on Skubal all start right about there. So this is not really a question of whether Detroit wants him back. It is a question of whether the Tigers will beat the biggest contract any pitcher has ever signed.
What a Tarik Skubal contract would cost the Detroit Tigers
ESPN's Kiley McDaniel surveyed 27 industry insiders on Oct. 2, and the average projection came back at eight years and $355 million, a $44.6 million average annual value. Sixteen of the 27, or 59 percent, landed between $325 million and $400 million over seven to 10 years. The full spread ran from four years and $176 million to 10 years and $500 million. SI's Tigers site put the number in that same $325 million to $400 million window.
Twenty-one of those 27 panelists expect Skubal to sign before Dec. 1, when the current collective bargaining agreement expires. The Dodgers and the New York Mets were named as true contenders, with the New York Yankees close behind and the Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and San Diego Padres listed as sleepers. Detroit was on the contender list too, which is the one part of this that should give Tigers fans something to hold onto.
Detroit already declined to pay him once
This is the hard part of the argument. Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris said after the deadline that the club had approached Skubal and his camp about an extension at one point, and that it was made clear to him Skubal wanted to reach free agency.
"Which is totally his right, and nobody should be upset about that," Harris said. He called it irresponsible not to move Skubal given the market for him, and he put the season on himself: "It's not on the players. It's not on the coaches. It's on me."
So a front office that would not get an extension done, and then traded him for prospects, is now being asked to outbid the Dodgers and the Mets at full price. Detroit does not just have to find the money. It has to explain the reversal.
Framber Valdez set the current Tigers ceiling
Detroit's largest pitching commitment is Framber Valdez, who signed a three-year, $115 million deal in February. His $38.3 million average annual value set a record for left-handed pitchers, and he can opt out after the second season. He was brought in to slot behind Skubal, and he is the top of the rotation now by default.
That is a real commitment. It is also not in the same conversation as $355 million over eight years. If the Tigers want to put a second front-line arm next to Valdez, Skubal is the best one available, and he is also the most expensive player on the board by a wide margin.
What the Tigers would be paying for
Skubal made 26 starts in 2026 between Detroit and Los Angeles and went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA. He threw 158 2/3 innings, gave up 126 hits and 52 runs, walked 27 and struck out 186, and finished with a 0.96 WHIP. He is 29 and turns 30 on Nov. 20, so the longest deals on the board would run deep into his 30s.
It would still be a major surprise if the Tigers gave Skubal a record-breaking contract. The money sits outside anything Detroit has shown it will spend on one player, and Harris already walked away from a smaller version of this decision. Someone is going to pay Skubal. Going on what the Tigers have already done, it is hard to see it being them.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Skubal & Kiké Headlight Dodgers 2027 Free Agent Class
item.dc:creator: Cody Snavely
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA—While the 2026 Major League Baseball postseason remains in play, the offseason has officially begun for the Los Angeles Dodgers after their anticlimactic series sweep at the hands of the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers. After the conclusion of the 2026 Fall Classic, the Dodgers are set to have a total of nine free agents hit the open market, an increase from five last season. While the list reads as nine, it is essentially eight, as veteran infielder Miguel Rojas annou
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA—While the 2026 Major League Baseball postseason remains in play, the offseason has officially begun for the Los Angeles Dodgers after their anticlimactic series sweep at the hands of the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers.
After the conclusion of the 2026 Fall Classic, the Dodgers are set to have a total of nine free agents hit the open market, an increase from five last season.
While the list reads as nine, it is essentially eight, as veteran infielder Miguel Rojas announced his retirement from Major League Baseball after the Dodgers’ Game Four loss.
Free Agents
(9): Blake Treinen, Evan Phillips, Kris Bubic, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández, Alex Vesia, Brusdar Graterol, Eric Lauer, Tarik Skubal
Blake Treinen
Veteran right-hander Blake Treinen’s season ended during the final week of September after a right shoulder setback that forced him off the Dodgers postseason roster.
Treinen returned to Los Angeles after his 2024 World Series heroics on a 2-year, $14 million contract, and now the 38-year-old will be without a home entering an offseason that may be the final season of his career.
Evan Phillips
Right-hander Evan Phillips missed all of 2025 and returned toward the middle of the 2026 regular season due to Tommy John surgery. However, in his games played, he was very effective, going 3-2 with a 3.46 ERA.
Still, Phillips will be entering his age 33 season and has already missed significant time due to right elbow/arm injuries, and with multiple pitchers in the pipeline, it’s not hard to see the Dodgers moving on.
Kris Bubic
Acquired at the trade deadline, left-hander Kris Bubic is likely to get a contract this Winter as a starter, since that was his primary role before injuries derailed his 2026 season.
Bubic was an All-Star in 2025 and, with a thin free-agent market, could land a nice contract from a team desperate for starting pitching.
Miguel Rojas
Shortly after the conclusion of Game Four of the NLCS, veteran utility infielder Miguel Rojas announced his retirement from Major League Baseball, bringing an end to his 13-year playing career.
Rojas is expected to remain with the Dodgers organization in a player devleopment/coaching role.
Kiké Hernández
October hero Kiké Hernández is hitting free agency yet again this Winter, and after a subpar performance in October, minus one huge home run off Chris Sale in the NLDS, not much is known about whether the Dodgers will try to run it back for another 1-year deal.
Overall, Hernández missed most of the season while recovering from elbow surgery and an oblique injury and hit 4 home runs in 90 at-bats while posting a below-average 82 OPS+.
The fan favorite will enter his age-36 season, likely ending his Dodgers tenure for the second time.
Alex Vesia
Arguably the biggest free agent from the Dodgers bullpen this Winter is left-hander Alex Vesia, who has likely pitched his way to a sizable multi-year contract that the Dodgers might not be inclined to match.
Vesia, 30, posted an elite 2.64 ERA and struck out 74 batters despite a below-average fastball velocity, but with backend pitching at a premium, his market is likely to be heavy.
Brusdar Graterol
Brusdar Graterol’s career has been defined by injuries, and that likely will force his time in Dodger Blue to come to an end this Winter.
Despite a 2.78 career ERA, the right-hander has pitched only 7.1 innings for the Dodgers since the 2024 regular season, missing the entire 2025 and 2026 seasons due to right shoulder surgery.
Eric Lauer
Like Bubic, left-hander Eric Lauer will enter the market as a starting pitcher, and after a second-half renaissance with the Dodgers, where he went 7-2 with a 4.50 ERA, he could be a dependable backend starter to eat innings for a variety of clubs.
Tarik Skubal
The consensus No. 1 free agent this Winter across baseball is two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, who is set to demand a massive multi-year contract that could go north of $400 million.
While the Dodgers will no doubt be involved, it’s hard to imagine them matching that while already having so many long-term deals tied up, especially in their starting rotation already.
Skubal is likely to sign before the MLB lockout on December 1st to maximize his contract, such as fellow Scott Boras client Corey Seager did after the 2021 season.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
Cody Snavely has been the co-editor of DodgersBeat and full-time host of the Bleed Los Podcast since February 2023. He has also written for multiple websites, such as Dodgers Way, Dodgers Low-Down, and Dodgers Tailgate. A Wilmington University graduate, Snavely is an avid Dodgers fan who uses his advanced baseball knowledge to keep fans updated on the latest storylines, rumors, and opinions on Dodgers baseball.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Blake Snell wastes no time putting together a Dodgers recruiting pitch to Tarik Skubal

Snell provided multiple quotes on Skubal, and each soundbite communicated his clear desire for the two-time Cy Young award-winner to stay in LA. “I would love nothing more than for him to be back," Snell said. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that ... so now that it’s over, don’t leave," Snell added about Skubal. But Sn
item.content:encoded:
In the difficult moments following the Los Angeles Dodgers' elimination last week, Blake Snell didn't hesitate to share his thoughts on Tarik Skubal. Snell provided multiple quotes on Skubal, and each soundbite communicated his clear desire for the two-time Cy Young award-winner to stay in LA.
“I would love nothing more than for him to be back," Snell said. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that ... so now that it’s over, don’t leave," Snell added about Skubal.
But Snell didn't stop at locker room chatter. He's now taken to social media in his attempts to keep Skubal around.
Blake Snell keeps publicly expressing his desire to keep Tarik Skubal on the Dodgers
Snell's efforts are light-hearted, though earnest, but it'll take something far more serious (in the form of hundreds of millions of dollars) for the Dodgers to ensure that the No. 1 free agent on the market returns to Los Angeles in 2027.
There's no doubt that Skubal fit into LA's clubhouse seamlessly in 2026. It also makes a ton of sense that Skubal and Snell get along, seeing as they are both Cy Young award-winning lefties who share an agent in Scott Boras.
Surely, Skubal can see himself happily returning to the Dodgers next season and moving forward with the organization. Nonetheless, he knows it wouldn't be wise to share his personal thoughts on his free agency, which is exactly why he's been mostly mum on the topic since the season ended. The lefty didn't get into his future at all following LA's elimination, even when prompted on multiple occasions by reporters.
The Dodgers will face multiple challenges when it comes to signing Tarik Skubal to a new deal
Beyond the looming lockout possibility and the uncertainty about the next collective bargaining agreement, the Dodgers will face sturdy competition for Skubal's services, most likely in the form of New York Mets owner Steve Cohen's deep pockets.
How will Andrew Friedman and the rest of LA's front office approach the Skubal situation? Will having fallen short of a three-peat add extra motivation to Friedman's mindset about getting a deal done for Skubal, or might he go in a different direction? Given how Friedman's operated in recent years, one assumes he'll go all-in on Skubal and do what he can to out-joust Cohen.
It's hard to imagine the Dodgers not playing a crucial role in the upcoming Skubal sweepstakes. It's also scary from a baseball perspective to think about how much more effective Skubal might be on the Dodgers next season once he's more comfortable with his new organization.
Per usual, the National League is hoping that the Dodgers don't get their guy. That's all good and fair, but Friedman probably has other plans. In other words, Snell's wishes have a good chance of coming true this winter.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Max Muncy compares Tarik Skubal to Clayton Kershaw on start days
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers took a big swing at the trade deadline to acquire Tarik Skubal, and although they fell short of a three-peat, the left-hander was instrumental to success they did have in the meantime. Not only was Skubal extremely valuable on the mound, but he also become a popular figure in the clubhouse. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers took a big swing at the trade deadline to acquire Tarik Skubal, and although they fell short of a three-peat, the left-hander was instrumental to success they did have in the meantime.
Not only was Skubal extremely valuable on the mound, but he also become a popular figure in the clubhouse. Part of that stems from how Skubal interacted with his teammates, even on days when he was the starting pitcher.
But how Skubal presents himself now was not always the case during his career. Instead, he often emulated behavior he saw from veterans in the Detroit Tigers’ clubhouse. That typically involved having headphones in and keeping to themselves. But at a certain point, he decided it would be more beneficial to be his authentic self instead.
“I just found it to be exhausting. I don’t think that’s who I am. It’s kind of putting on a facade,” Skubal recently explained. “You’re just not yourself. I didn’t feel like myself when I was doing that, putting headphones in and trying to be focused. I found myself mentally exhausted in the second or third innings of games.
“And I’m like, ‘Why am I tired today? I should be ready to go.’ When I got hurt in ’22, I decided enough is enough. I’m caring way too much about all the little things that don’t really matter, don’t really impact the game of baseball.
“I don’t know if it’s like superstitious, but like making sure the music is the right setting, making sure the music is the right songs at the right time, and you’re just caring about all the wrong things, I think. For me it was mentally freeing to take my headphones off and just be who I am and interact with guys.
“As it gets closer to game time, you get ready to go and you’re going to go out there and compete. But I just didn’t really find much of a benefit of trying to be locked in four hours before a game. I want to be myself. Then I’ll lock in as the game gets closer.”
Max Muncy compares Tarik Skubal to Clayton Kershaw
For the Dodgers players who have been around awhile, including Max Muncy, Skubal’s approach represented a drastic departure from what they would normally see from a pitcher like Clayton Kershaw.
“For me with starting pitchers, when it’s their start day, it’s always kind of an interesting debacle, we’ll call it,” Muncy began when asked about Skubal’s demeanor.
“With him, I’ve never seen somebody be so normal on a start day. To me that’s really refreshing and really awesome to see. He doesn’t change his attitude or his mind, the way he acts in the clubhouse with the other guys. For a guy to be as competitive as he is on the mound and as fiery as he is, it’s really awesome to see how he goes about every other day exactly the same. That’s pretty rare to see.”
Muncy noticed a difference between the two pitchers from Skubal’s first start for the Dodgers.
“[Skubal] came up to me and started asking me questions and talking about something that wasn’t even involved in the game. I don’t remember what it was, but he was talking about something and it just completely threw me off,” Muncy recalled. “Like you said, playing with Kersh for all those years, it’s the complete opposite.
“That’s where I go to the word ‘debacle’ a bit. Us position players always laugh about the starting pitchers just because could you imagine if we acted that way every time we had to start on the field? Those are the main guys. They have their routines, and they’re that way for a reason. You can’t win games without them.
“So you really need the starting pitching. Whatever routine they want to go with and whatever show they want to put on, we’re here for all of it. Yeah, Scoobs and Kersh couldn’t be more opposite in terms of their start day routine.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made one of the most anticipated moves of 2026 ahead of the trade deadline by trading for two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal, the ace of the Detroit Tigers.
Since Skubal was traded on an expiring contract, there is no guarantee that he will be back on the Dodgers in 2027. LA has been predicted to compete with six teams that would potentially offer the southpaw a deal this offseason — one that is expected to potentially exceed $400 million.
Skubal spoke after last week's postseason exit on what it meant to play for the Dodgers this summer, and though it is no indication of what the financial side of things will look like this offseason, provided a glowing review on the organization.
“I mean, incredible organization, incredible teammates, incredible fanbase,” Skubal said. “Honored to wear the LA across your chest and on the hat. Doesn’t make this feel any better. It sucks, but I think everybody in here gave it everything they had, and sometimes that’s just baseball."
Skubal made 10 regular season starts after the trade and totaled a 2.61 ERA in that span. Over 11 postseason innings (two starts), he had a 2.45 ERA, throwing 14 strikeouts to four walks.
In other news, veteran utility star Kiké Hernández recently spoke on his future as he becomes a free agent once again this offseason. The fan favorite made his intentions known when speaking to reporters after last week's National League Championship Series elimination.
"I would love to have one more try, trying to win another one," Hernández said. "But I don't really know what's going to happen. I hope I'm back, and if I'm not, I hope that I get to play for a winning team."
Finally, among the many free agents on the team, there is one that the Dodgers simply can't afford to lose. Alternatively, there is also one that, according to the team at Dodgers On SI, LA can afford to let walk.

The New York Yankees have several paths they could take in free agency this offseason.
If history repeats itself, they will be quite successful.
One of the top names floating is that of Tarik Skubal of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Do the Yankees stand a chance?
Yankees Prediction Points To Skubal Opportunity
Christopher Kline of FanSided unveiled his latest rankings of Skubal's potential landing spots.
Of the eight teams he mentioned, New York comes in at No. 4.
This isn't a bad spot to be for an organization that generally thrives on its perfectly imperfect starting rotation.
But that certainly doesn't mean they're the most likely ballclub to acquire to veteran southpaw.
"It would require Hal Steinbrenner and the front office to basically sign off on a blank check, but the Yankees' ALDS loss to the Rays was a sobering defeat," Kline explained. "There are cracks in the foundation. Many of those cracks are injury-related and concentrated in the lineup; Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón is as strong a four-man gauntlet as any rotation in MLB. The Yankees also have Ryan Weathers, Will Warren and top prospects like Elmer Rodríguez and Carlos Lagrange for depth.
"Still, the Yankees know the importance of depth, especially as their non-Schlittler core ages and becomes more injury-prone. Skubal provides stability and instantly lends credibility to any postseason aspirations. Schlittler-Skubal becomes the most fearsome pitching duo in baseball. Never say never."
Sobering is perhaps the best way to describe how their campaign ended.
Taking it a step further, the value of depth became all the more clear for the Yankees after their star slugger Aaron Judge was sidelined for much of the season.
This forced New York to rely on their younger stars who tend to play in the shadows.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers have one major advantage the Mets can't offer Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Drew Koch
item.description: Tarik Skubal will get a head start in free agency after the Los Angeles Dodgers were unable to find a way to overcome the Milwaukee Brewers during Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. The loss ended the Dodgers' aspirations of a three-peat, and effectively started Skubal's free agency clock. The Dodgers traded for Skubal at this year's deadline, shipping top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope and pitcher River Ryan to the Detroit Tigers in exchange for the two-time Cy Y
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal will get a head start in free agency after the Los Angeles Dodgers were unable to find a way to overcome the Milwaukee Brewers during Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. The loss ended the Dodgers' aspirations of a three-peat, and effectively started Skubal's free agency clock.
The Dodgers traded for Skubal at this year's deadline, shipping top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope and pitcher River Ryan to the Detroit Tigers in exchange for the two-time Cy Young award-winner. Though most observers expect LA to be heavily involved in his free agency during the offseason, they won't be the club vying for his services.
SNY MLB insider Chelsea Janes is reporting that the New York Mets are expected to match whatever offer Skubal receives this winter. This is hardly surprising, as most intel has linked the Dodgers and Mets as the two most likely teams to sign the left-hander this offseason. A dark horse or two is sure to emerge, but for all intents and purposes, the pursuit of Skubal will end with one of these two teams.
Both Los Angeles and New York have deep pockets, and Skubal will undoubtedly be seeking to sign the largest deal for a starting pitcher in the history of Major League Baseball. Look for the eventual deal to be worth upwards of $400 million, surpassing the 12-year, $325 million deal Yoshinodu Yamamoto signed in 2024.
But the Dodgers can offer something the Mets can't — a consistent opportunity to win a World Series championship.
While LA's hopes of a three-peat were dashed by Milwaukee, Dodgers fans know that Andrew Friedman will be quick to restock the roster with hopes of returning to the Fall Classic in 2027.
The Dodgers are better positioned than the Mets for long-term success
Regardless of how the upcoming Collective Bargaining negotiations turn out, it's difficult to see any type of resolution between the owners and the Players Association that drastically affects LA's chances to compete for a world title for the foreseeable future. The Dodgers still have the best player in baseball (Shohei Ohtani) under contract, and rotation (Yamamoto, Ohtani, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow) is already top-notch, even without Skubal.
The Mets, on the other hand, haven't won a World Series since 1986. Even last season, with All-Stars like Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Pete Alonso, New York was beaten out by a Cincinnati Reds team that won just 83 games to qualify for the playoffs. The Mets came into this season with high expectations, but ended the year in the NL East basement.
It's highly unlikely that Skubal will find that type atomsphere enticing, espeically if there are similar offers on the table from the Dodgers or another high-dollar suitor.
Despite Steve Cohen's excessive spending, few organizations in Major League Baseball are less appealing than the Mets. New York has endured six losing seasons over the last 10 years. While some stars don't mind playing second fiddle to the New York Yankees and getting bounced from the postseason during the second week of September, Skubal seems to enjoy LA's winning culture.

item.title: [FanSided] Ranking Tarik Skubal suitors from favorites to dark horses
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline
item.description: Tarik Skubal and the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept out of the NLCS by the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers, a refreshing change of pace after two years of Dodgers dominance — and a helpful reminder to the MLB owners that payroll alone does not determine winning. item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal and the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept out of the NLCS by the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers, a refreshing change of pace after two years of Dodgers dominance — and a helpful reminder to the MLB owners that payroll alone does not determine winning. It also leaves Skubal with a more difficult decision in free agency than many expected.
The Dodgers will not re-sign Skubal before the lockout in December, as there's simply too much risk without knowing how the salary cap will function come 2027. Really regardless of how MLB's labor dispute plays out, however, Los Angeles will hope to retain Skubal, who is still rightly regarded as the most bankable ace in baseball. The question is: Are the Dodgers the favorites for his services? Let's rank all realistic suitors, from least to most realistic.
8. Philadelphia Phillies
The Phillies are desperate and the Phillies typically spend money. Not necessarily as liberally as fans would like, but it's not impossible to imagine Dave Dombrowski — with the World Series window closing rapidly on this aging core — deciding that Skubal is worth an all-in push.
It would give Philadelphia the most talented rotation in MLB between Skubal, Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sánchez, Jesús Luzardo and Aaron Nola, four of whom could compete for NL Cy Young next season. There's also Andrew Painter, a former top prospect who came into his own down the stretch and delivered big outs in the postseason, to provide depth.
The Phillies probably have enough money wrapped up in that rotation (and in Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber and Trea Turner) to be turned off of paying Skubal top dollar, but it's a fun thought for a team hoping to lean even more on run prevention moving forward.
7. Boston Red Sox
The Red Sox wielded one of the deepest and most reliable rotations in MLB last season; that was with top ace Garrett Crochet on the IL. Upon Crochet's return, Boston will have a compelling blend of experience (Crochet, Ranger Suárez) and emerging youth (Payton Tolle, Jake Bennett) to throw at their opponents.
Then again, they know the toll injuries can take, and Sonny Gray — probably their best regular season starter this past season — is now a free agent. The Red Sox could simply line up a new contract for Gray and be content, but why not aim higher? Skubal has proven remarkably durable over the years and he offers Boston a much longer window as Crochet's partner in crime. Suddenly, the Red Sox have the best one-two punch in baseball and it wouldn't be especially close.
After the Yankees lit them up in the Wild Card round (and after Boston's top arms couldn't pitch deep into either postseason game), there's pressure for a big swing.
6. Chicago Cubs
There's no doubting the Cubs' ability to generate offense, but the rotation has been a sore spot for years now. Jed Hoyer has shown a great appetite for spending in free agency of late; the Alex Bregman signing was a real flex. That said, Chicago needs to allocate more resources toward pitching. The Edward Cabrera trade went belly up. Shōta Imanaga is a free agent now, as are trade deadline pickups Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes.
Chicago will get help internally with both Cade Horton and Justin Steele returning from season-long elbow injuries; Ben Brown, who finally broke out in 2026, should also be back in the mix. Beyond them, however, it's pretty grim. Matthew Boyd and Javier Assad can eat innings in the regular season, but neither has proven able to pitch deep in October — at least not consistently.
Skubal would deliver Chicago the frontline ace it has long lacked, with a solid scaffolding of talent behind him. The Cubs would be much better positioned to challenge Milwaukee in the division and potentially emerge from a crowded National League field.
5. Detroit Tigers
Skubal has made it clear he would've spent his entire career in Detroit if it was up to him. All the Tigers need to do is come through with a competitive offer. While last year's surprise Framber Valdez signing was a positive indication of the front office's competitive intent, there's a reason no Skubal extension ever came to fruition — or even remotely close.
A client of Scott Boras, Skubal was never inclined to sign an extension. But the Tigers' offers weren't even in the parking lot, much less the ballpark. Detroit will need to scale up its ambition significantly if it wants to lure Skubal back to the midwest.
All that said, Skubal has an affection for Detroit that's worth mentioning. The Tigers also desperately need a frontline ace in Skubal's mold. Young bucks like Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan are very talented, but the Tigers don't really have an established vet besides Valdez, who was a mess last season.
4. New York Yankees
The Yankees tend to flex their muscles in free agency, although with diminishing returns in recent years. New York is no longer the most lucrative destination for a lot of A-tier stars. Juan Soto a couple years ago, Kyle Tucker last winter; the Yankees are getting outbid pretty consistently these days. That has not stopped New York from stockpiling stars, though, especially in the rotation.
It would require Hal Steinbrenner and the front office to basically sign off on a blank check, but the Yankees' ALDS loss to the Rays was a sobering defeat. There are cracks in the foundation. Many of those cracks are injury-related and concentrated in the lineup; Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón is as strong a four-man gauntlet as any rotation in MLB. The Yankees also have Ryan Weathers, Will Warren and top prospects like Elmer Rodríguez and Carlos Lagrange for depth.
Still, the Yankees know the importance of depth, especially as their non-Schlittler core ages and becomes more injury-prone. Skubal provides stability and instantly lends credibility to any postseason aspirations. Schlittler-Skubal becomes the most fearsome pitching duo in baseball. Never say never.
3. Toronto Blue Jays
The Blue Jays have steadily become the most aggressive front office in the American League. After finishing runner-up in the Juan Soto and Shohei Ohtani sweepstakes, Toronto extended Vladimir Guerrero Jr. at a $500 million price point and signed Dylan Cease in the early days of free agency last winter. A disappointing season should not preclude Toronto from maintaining its all-in approach; if anything, it's more motivation for the Blue Jays to stack talent. This team was in the World Series a year ago.
Toronto is a great market, with a vibrant local culture and an entire country behind the Blue Jays. That ought to appeal to the vanity of a star like Skubal, who would team up with the projected AL Cy Young runner-up in Cease. The Jays also made a savvy trade for José Soriano at the deadline, adding another premium arm in his prime. Trey Yesavage, once healthy, could resume his ascent to stardom. The talent is there.
Skubal solidifies Toronto as a legitimate World Series contender coming into 2027. Moreover, the Jays have a lot of money coming off the books, which should free up the front office to spend recklessly where it counts. Toronto is always the "dark horse" in these top-dollar bidding wars, but ruling out the Blue Jays would be foolish.
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
It's impossible to rule out the incumbents. Los Angeles made the Skubal trade in part because of their deep farm system — and in part because it set the stage for a potential long-term partnership. There's a reason small-market front offices were unwilling to match L.A.'s outgoing package (see: Brewers). The Dodgers could afford to trade two of the 50ish best prospects in baseball because the team can feel reasonably good about both competing for a World Series this season (oh well) and re-signing Skubal when he hits the open market.
An NLCS loss does complicate the situation somewhat, not to mention the unknowability of upcoming labor disputes. The Dodgers' loss was a direct result of investing hundreds of millions of dollars in stars who are beginning to decline. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Shohei Ohtani, Will Smith, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell are all on the wrong side of 30; Tucker will join that list next season. Los Angeles will endure more and more diminishing returns.
That said, nothing (besides a strict salary cap) can really stop the Dodgers from compensating for declining stars by signing more expensive stars, even if it leaves the cap sheet in utter chaos five years from now. That has been L.A.'s strategy to date; it was part of the logic behind the Skubal trade. The Dodgers still arguably represent Skubal's best chance to win a World Series, which will no doubt be part of the calculus if another team can't dramatically outspend them.
1. New York Mets
If any team can blow L.A.'s offer out of the water, it's the Mets. Steve Cohen is baseball's richest owner and New York has consistently tossed its hat in the ring for MLB's premium free agents. Juan Soto's $765 million contract set a new record; Skubal very well could set a record for pitchers.
The Mets are coming off of a last-place season, too, which only fuels anxiety in the fan base. It should also fuel aggression in the front office. David Stearns is under pressure to prove that he has what it takes to win in New York. Skubal would join an emerging ace in Nolan McLean, plus other whippersnappers like Zac Thornton and Jonah Tong. The Mets need depth besides, as Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea look more like bullpen arms these days. New York, however, is the one non-Dodgers team with enough money to sign Skubal and pursue other targets.
If the Dodgers get spooked by the shadow of their own payroll, which is more likely than ever, the Mets are the logical team we can expect to swoop in and win the Skubal bidding war outright.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] "I’ll Die on That Hill”: Dodgers Face a Tough Shohei Ohtani Call After World Series Dreams Fall Apart
item.dc:creator: Utsav Gupta
item.description: Shohei Ohtani, the two-way star for the Los Angeles Dodgers, posted a 1.79 ERA as a pitcher but managed just five hits in 26 postseason at-bats. One Dodgers analyst believes the path forward requires a radical shift in how the team uses its star as the Dodgers face an uncomfortable choice: keep Ohtani as a two-way star or unlock his full potential as a hitter. The Brewers' NLCS sweep eliminated the Dodgers from World Series contention, forcing the organization to reassess Ohtani's role. Doug McK
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani, the two-way star for the Los Angeles Dodgers, posted a 1.79 ERA as a pitcher but managed just five hits in 26 postseason at-bats. One Dodgers analyst believes the path forward requires a radical shift in how the team uses its star as the Dodgers face an uncomfortable choice: keep Ohtani as a two-way star or unlock his full potential as a hitter.
The Brewers' NLCS sweep eliminated the Dodgers from World Series contention, forcing the organization to reassess Ohtani's role. Doug McKain (@DMAC_LA), a Dodgers personality, said in this Thursday night episode of Dodgers Dugout.
"So I will take it to my grave. I will die on that hill. If the Dodgers had the best version of Shohei Ohtani, the hitter, like we saw last year, they would have beaten the Brewers. They would have won the World Series," McKain said.
The sweep revealed a struggling batter who had lost his form. Ohtani hit just .160/.284/.253 in 88 plate appearances following August 18, striking out ten times in October. His Game 4 three-run shot was his first long ball in 26 games.
Two-way players historically struggle with workload management. Ohtani's June knee injury, followed by poor hitting, suggests the dual role may have contributed to his decline.
Ohtani offered a more measured perspective following the loss. According to MLB.com, Ohtani responded through interpreter Will Ireton.
"Yes, definitely. And looking forward to having a better season next year," Ohtani said.
His ERA stood at 1.79 with a .179 opponent batting average over 85 2/3 innings, and only Jim Palmer, Jacob deGrom, and Clayton Kershaw have a lower ERA than Ohtani in their careers.
However, Ohtani's pitching durability became a concern when knee problems emerged on June 11, and over his next four starts, he allowed 12 earned runs in 24 2/3 innings after allowing just five in his first 61.
Ohtani has started and ended an MLB season as a two-way player only twice, in 2021 and 2022. Injuries derailed him in 2018 and 2023, with elbow problems in both seasons.
McKain took this logic further during the same Dodgers Dugout broadcast by saying, "If getting the best version of Shohei Ohtani the hitter means he's a one-way player, then that's what's best for the Los Angeles Dodgers."
The argument gains weight because the lineup, not the rotation, sank this club. The Dodgers have a .148 batting average with runners in scoring position during the NLCS. They were out-homered 7-1, and their catcher, Will Smith, went 3-for-31 in the postseason.
However, the pitching record remains valid. Dodgers' right-handed Tyler Glasnow and left-handed Blake Snell threw only 116 2/3 innings during the regular season, while Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the only pitcher qualified for the rotation.
The rotation picture could shift again this winter. Tarik Skubal, the left-handed pitcher acquired at the deadline, might depart in free agency, leaving Yamamoto and the unpredictable Ohtani to lead a rotation already short on innings.
The Dodgers are well aware of this dilemma. According to Katie Woo of The Athletic, Andrew Friedman, the president of baseball operations, commented before the playoffs that Ohtani's historic position takes a great toll on the organization.
"What he's doing is unprecedented, and it takes a real toll," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said before the postseason. "It's unprecedented for all of us, and we're kind of feeling our way through it together."
There might be another way. The Dodgers could rest Ohtani for several months before ramping him up to full participation, even though there is still uncertainty about the surgery he may need for a knee or biceps injury.
Timing is key. Ohtani turns 32 soon, has seven years remaining on his deal, and the Dodgers need him healthy for the playoffs, not just April.

item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres were able to get into the playoffs after what was a shaky start to the 2026 MLB season, but the team fell short of its goal to win the World Series.
San Diego lost in four games to the Milwaukee Brewers, seeing another year go by without a title, sending this team into a crucial offseason. The Padres' front office will have a lot to figure out this offseason, especially within the starting rotation, with key players hitting free agency.
Padres Linked With Tarik Skubal
One name that has started to generate some buzz around the Padres as the offseason gets going is ace Tarik Skubal, who split time with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Detroit Tigers. San Diego could look to go after Skubal, giving their rotation a major boost for the future.
MLB analyst Zachary D. Rymer of Bleacher Report recently ranked landing spots for Skubal in a new piece. Within this, Rymer listed the Padres as a top landing spot, and the fit does make a lot of sense.
"If ever there was a way to show they mean business, it's by signing Skubal away from those darn Dodgers. Maybe it wouldn't totally undo the little brother vs. big brother dynamic between the two NL West powers, but it would give the Padres a real trump card: the best pitcher in baseball.
"Besides, the Padres are going to need Skubal if Michael King declines his $28 million player option for 2027 and becomes a free agent. Skubal is one of the few pitchers in MLB who would represent an upgrade over King, even if signing him would likely cost more than $40 million per year," Rymer wrote.
The Padres have spent a lot of money in the last few offseasons, which has backfired on this franchise at times. It has seen the team allow multiple stars to leave town, pushing back what the ceiling of this organization could be.
Skubal could change the entire starting rotation for the Padres this offseason, but he is expected to receive a deal over $300 million, if not closer to $400 million. San Diego has given out large contracts in the past, but this would be a new precedent for this team.
Should the Padres Go After Tarik Skubal?
On the field, the Padres should absolutely do whatever it takes to bring Skubal to San Diego. But the money is will be another question that this organization is going to have to grapple with.
With the new ownership in place, the Padres are expected to keep spending, but giving Skubal what he wants could be tough. San Diego has a lot of heavy contracts on the books already, and handing out another could be a big swing for this team.
Overall, the Padres will be involved in the Skubal sweepstakes, especially with how president of baseball operations A.J. Preller operates. Nobody can count out San Diego in this process, but other teams could present an easier path to give the lefty ace the type of deal that he is looking for this winter.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Blake Snell Is NOT Beating The Ring Chasing Allegations” – MLB Fans React After Dodgers Veteran’s ‘Don’t Leave’ Message To Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Nancy Singh
item.description: MLB fans have taken a dig at Blake Snell after the Dodgers pitcher urged Tarik Skubal to remain in Los Angeles following the team's National League Championship Series elimination. The Dodgers' bid for a third consecutive championship ended with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. item.content:encoded:
MLB fans have taken a dig at Blake Snell after the Dodgers pitcher urged Tarik Skubal to remain in Los Angeles following the team's National League Championship Series elimination.
The Dodgers' bid for a third consecutive championship ended with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. Skubal, who was traded to Los Angeles from the Detroit Tigers earlier in the season, is now set to become one of the most sought-after free agents this offseason.
Following the Dodgers' elimination, Snell shared his thoughts on Skubal's future in an interview with the California Post. The left-hander expressed his desire to continue playing alongside his friend and urged him not to leave the team.
"I just said, he can't leave me, especially on these terms. The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren't able to do that … So now that it's over, it's like, 'Don't leave. He's just a great human, great pitcher. Fun to learn from. Fun to have conversations with. Just talk baseball with. I would love nothing more than for him to be back," said Snell.
However, his comments drew a skeptical response from some fans on Reddit, with one user suggesting Snell was more interested in keeping a talented teammate around to improve the Dodgers' championship chances.
"Snell is NOT beating the ring-chasing allegations."
Mocking Snell's message, another user wrote:
Suggesting that Snell wants to make the chase easier, another follower penned:
Along similar lines, a few other fans chimed in:
Skubal split his 2026 season between Detroit and Los Angeles after undergoing elbow surgery that sidelined him for six weeks. Across 26 appearances, he recorded a 12-7 record with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts over 158.2 innings.
Blake Snell reflected on the Dodgers' NLCS elimination
Following the Dodgers' 6-4 loss to the Brewers in the deciding game of the NLCS on Thursday, Blake Snell acknowledged that Milwaukee had played better baseball throughout the series during his post-game interview. He also admitted that the elimination was painful but expressed confidence that the team could learn from the defeat.
"You know, we got everything we had, they're just the better team and, yeah, it's pretty true. I mean, they played really good baseball, they played better baseball than us, and no, it's just, it was a good series, you know, that was everything we had, and they're just better, but losing is never fun, and it definitely hurts, but it'll make us better. I mean, I love our team, I love everything about it honestly, so I just think we are gonna get better," said Blake Snell.
The Dodgers pitcher also expressed confidence that the team would use the offseason to improve and prepare for the 2027 campaign.

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Irá L.A. tras Skubal? Las interrogantes que enfrentan los Dodgers en esta temporada baja

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES - La temporada baja ha llegado antes de lo previsto para los Dodgers.
Antes de haber asimilado por completo la derrota del jueves por la noche (6-4) ante los Cerveceros en el Juego 4 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional —resultado que puso fin a su temporada y a su intento de lograr un tercer título consecutivo—, los Dodgers tuvieron que afrontar la realidad de que probablemente se avecinan cambios en el equipo.
Los Dodgers perderán a nueve jugadores debido a la agencia libre, un grupo encabezado por la figura más destacada del mercado, Tarik Skubal. Los otros jugadores que pronto serán agentes libres son el venezolano Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández, Evan Phillips, Alex Vesia, Blake Treinen, Eric Lauer, Kris Bubic y el venezolano Brusdar Graterol.
Gran parte del núcleo del equipo de Los Ángeles permanecerá intacto en el futuro previsible, por lo que la ventana competitiva no se está cerrando; sin embargo, este podría ser un periodo de transición entre una era del béisbol de los Dodgers y otra.
"Nunca puedes pensar que este es el final", dijo Rojas, quien permanecerá en la organización desempeñando un papel en el desarrollo de jugadores. "Y conozco muy bien a esta organización; no se conformarán con esta derrota".
A lo largo de 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, los Dodgers han encontrado formas fluidas de incorporar talento joven a sus plantillas para complementar a su núcleo de veteranos experimentados. Ese proceso ya ha comenzado con el dominicano Josue De Paula —el prospecto número 4 a nivel general según MLB Pipeline—, así como con el receptor suplente Dalton Rushing y el jugador de cuadro Alex Freeland.
No obstante, es posible que los Dodgers deban adoptar un enfoque más deliberado para asignar roles más destacados a sus jugadores jóvenes de cara al futuro, lo que dará lugar a decisiones interesantes durante esta temporada baja.
"No conocemos el futuro", comentó el dominicano Teóscar Hernández. "Pero algo que sabemos es que nos preocupamos los unos por los otros, nos cuidamos mutuamente y nos apoyamos durante todo el año... Este grupo es realmente especial, no por lo que hemos logrado en los últimos dos años y en este, sino simplemente por la unión que tenemos".
A continuación, un vistazo a algunas de las decisiones más importantes sobre el roster que deberán tomar los Dodgers durante esta temporada baja:
¿Participarán en la puja por Skubal?
Los Dodgers se desprendieron de dos prospectos clasificados entre los 100 mejores —el abridor listo para las Grandes Ligas River Ryan y el jardinero Zyhir Hope—, además del lanzador derecho Brady Smith, a cambio de contar con Skubal por un periodo de hasta tres meses. No fueron el único equipo dispuesto a hacer una gran inversión por un talento del calibre de Skubal, y lo mismo ocurrirá cuando este llegue al mercado de agentes libres por primera vez.
Skubal ganó su caso de arbitraje salarial contra los Tigres la temporada baja pasada, obteniendo un salario récord de US$32 millones. Se espera ampliamente que consiga la mayor cantidad de dinero garantizado jamás otorgada a un lanzador en la agencia libre, superando el contrato de 12 años y US$325 millones de Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
En su año previo a la agencia libre, Skubal se perdió seis semanas tras someterse a una cirugía en el codo izquierdo, pero aun así completó otra campaña sólida, registrando una marca de 12-7 y una efectividad de 2.72 en 26 aperturas con los Tigres y los Dodgers. Prefirió no hablar sobre su futuro inmediatamente después de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional (SCLN).
"Sí, realmente no voy a hacer comentarios sobre mi futuro", dijo Skubal. "El día de hoy es una porquería, ya sabes, y en eso es en lo que estoy pensando ahora mismo".
Aun así, Skubal expresó su agradecimiento por el tiempo que pasó con los Dodgers.
"Una organización increíble, compañeros increíbles, una afición increíble", dijo. "Es un honor llevar las letras 'L.A.' en el pecho y en la gorra".
¿Cómo le darán tiempo de juego para De Paula?
En septiembre, De Paula hizo que el salto de Doble-A a las Grandes Ligas pareciera sencillo, impresionando tanto a los Dodgers que logró entrar en el roster de postemporada como opción de bateador emergente. Sin embargo, su limitación radicaba en que el equipo de Grandes Ligas lo veía únicamente como bateador designado, una posición ocupada por Shohei Ohtani.
"Creo que la mejora que Josue mostró en los jardines entre 2025 y 2026 es real", comentó el mes pasado Andrew Friedman, presidente de operaciones de béisbol. "Y para nosotros, se trata de dar otro gran paso de cara a 2027. Él tiene las herramientas y la capacidad para lograrlo".
Con el tiempo, los Dodgers tendrán que poner a De Paula a jugar en los jardines. No obstante, sus jardineros titulares —Teóscar Hernández, el cubano Andy Pages y Kyle Tucker— tienen contrato vigente hasta la próxima temporada.
Si los Dodgers consideran que De Paula está listo para ser jugador titular habitual, eso probablemente implicaría, como mínimo, limitar el tiempo de juego de Hernández. También podría darse una medida más drástica: buscar un equipo interesado en asumir la última temporada garantizada de su contrato de tres años y US$66 millones.
Otra opción sería que De Paula comenzara la temporada en Triple-A, donde podría trabajar en su defensa en un entorno de menor presión.
¿Qué jugadores veteranos clave regresarán?
Entre los agentes libres inminentes, algunas de las bajas más significativas en cuanto a liderazgo serían Kiké Hernández, Phillips, Vesia y Treinen. El bullpen ciertamente podría tener hueco para lanzadores de situaciones críticas como Phillips y Vesia, pero el encaje de Hernández entre los jugadores de posición no está tan claro.
Hernández, el propio "Mr. October" de los Dodgers, tuvo una temporada regular marcada por las lesiones. Tampoco estuvo a la altura de su habitual rendimiento en postemporada, conectando apenas un jonrón solitario en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional (SDLN) como único imparable. Es una figura importante en el vestuario y, aunque le encantaría volver a Los Ángeles, sabe que sus necesidades y las del equipo deben coincidir durante la agencia libre.
"Me encantaría intentarlo una vez más, tratar de ganar otro", dijo Hernández. "Pero realmente no sé qué va a pasar. Espero volver y, si no es así, espero poder jugar en un equipo ganador".

item.title: [Around the Foghorn] SF Giants have one minor advantage over Dodgers when it comes to Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Nick San Miguel
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have been eliminated from the playoffs which is always good news for the SF Giants. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been eliminated from the playoffs which is always good news for the SF Giants. Now the biggest question for LA becomes whether they will bring back left-handed ace Tarik Skubal who is going to be the top free agent on the market.
The assumption is that the Dodgers probably will sign him since they sign basically all of the good free agents with their seemingly infinite wealth which potentially could be due to nefarious business practices from owner Mark Walter. Lockout, anyone?
But I digress. The Dodgers are obviously the favorite for Skubal, but the Giants cannot be counted out entirely because they have one minor advantage over LA and every other MLB team: they’re the closest to where Skubal grew up.
The 29-year-old two-time Cy Young Award winner was born in Hayward, California. He grew up an Oakland A’s fan which makes sense for a native of the East Bay, but if any part of him is nostalgic for the Bay Area and he wants to come home then the Giants are the only game in town with the A’s headed to Las Vegas.
It’s not a major advantage by any stretch. Odds are Skubal cares a lot more about how much money teams are offering or whether he will be joining a contender or not, but sometimes a return home can be a really big motivating factor for players in free agency.
Giants may not be willing to spend enough to land Tarik Skubal
The question is really whether the Giants would be willing to offer Skubal the amount of money it is likely to take to lure him back to the Bay Area. History says no since Giants chairman Greg Johnson has been very blunt in recent years about how the team is not keen on paying top dollar for the biggest free agent starters. Maybe the 2026 season will force him to change his tune on that, but we will have to hold our breath on that one.
It’s going to be hard for the Giants to compete with teams that have a lot of money and are ready to contend right now. Even if the Giants offered Skubal the most money he might have reservations about joining a team that only won 65 games this season.
Giants fans already know it’s probably best to not get our hopes up when it comes to a big fish like Skubal, but maybe a return to the Bay Area could convince him to shock everyone and sign with San Francisco.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Blake Snell Makes Emotional Pitch for Tarik Skubal to Stay With Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers star Tarik Skubal is officially available to sign with any team, ending his two-month run with the Dodgers, though Blake Snell does not want to see him go. When the Dodgers traded for Skubal, they knew the deal: Skubal would hit the free-agent market as the best player, and he had a decent chance of leaving to pitch elsewhere. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Tarik Skubal is officially available to sign with any team, ending his two-month run with the Dodgers, though Blake Snell does not want to see him go.
When the Dodgers traded for Skubal, they knew the deal: Skubal would hit the free-agent market as the best player, and he had a decent chance of leaving to pitch elsewhere.
However, the Dodgers hoped they would at least reach the World Series, where he could see the franchise’s complete success.
Snell’s pitch to Skubal
Now, he is free to leave after a devastating NLCS, though someone he calls his brother doesn’t want to see him go.
Blake Snell, who has formed a very tight bond with Skubal, already made his pitch after the team was eliminated.
“I just said, he can’t leave me, especially on these terms,” Snell told the California Post. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that … So now that it’s over, it’s like, ‘Don’t leave.’”
Snell and Skubal were regularly pictured together in the dugout or in the clubhouse celebrations after clinching a victory.
Both elite pitchers, they take their preparation seriously and enjoy talking about the art of pitching, and their personalities sync so well that Snell has a true friend.
“He’s just a great human, great pitcher. Fun to learn from. Fun to have conversations with. Just talk baseball with,” Snell said.
“I would love nothing more than for him to be back.
Can the Dodgers re-sign Tarik Skubal?
The Dodgers have the money to sign Skubal, and if they want to keep their immense starting-pitching edge, they could allocate resources there.
The big priority will be adding younger bats and new energy to the lineup, though with their farm system and shipping away some players, the Dodgers could do that without spending big.
Instead, they could opt to sign Skubal and enter the season with another great rotation.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers pitcher already started recruiting Tarik Skubal to re-sign
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: The offseason has come earlier than the Los Angeles Dodgers would have liked this year following their loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. item.content:encoded:
The offseason has come earlier than the Los Angeles Dodgers would have liked this year following their loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series.
The vast majority of the players from the 2026 roster will carry over into next season, with one potential exceptionin Tarik Skual. He declined to discuss plans regarding free agency following the Dodgers’ Game 4 loss.
While Skubal declined to comment, Blake Snell told Jack Harris of the California Post that he already begun his recruitment pitch in hopes of convincing the Dodgers’ trade deadline acquisition to stick around.
“I just said, he can’t leave me, especially on these terms,” Snell told the California Post, following the Dodgers’ elimination in the National League Championship Series. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that … So now that it’s over, it’s like, ‘Don’t leave.’”
It is safe to say Skubal would be the Dodgers’ top free agency target if Snell were leading the charge.
“I would love nothing more,” Snell said, “than for him to be back.”
Although Skubal had only been with the Dodgers for a short time, he quickly endeared himself to his new teammates in the clubhouse.
The relationship building had been a two-way street, with Skubal expressing how much he enjoyed his experience with the Dodgers organization.
Getting more comfortable in his new surroundings was a factor to Skubal finding a better rhythm down the stretch of the season after initially falling short of lofty expectations.
The Dodgers presumably will have some level of interest in re-signing Skubal, but how aggressive they will — or can be — may hinge on the economics set forth in a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA).
Tarik Skubal’s playoff starts
At the time of discussing the Dodgers’ trade for Skubal, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said he could not wait to see the 29-year-old on the mound come October.
“I will say obviously watching playoff baseball outside of when the Dodgers play, is fun for me. You don’t have a rooting interest, you can sit back and enjoy the theater of October baseball,” Friedman said at the time. “Watching Tarik Skubal pitch in the playoffs last year was must-see TV.
“I was in awe watching the energy, the dominance he exhibited there, and I can’t wait to see it in Dodger Blue.”
Unfortunately, Skubal wasn’t able to be fully dominant in his two playoff outings. Though, he did record seven strikeouts in both starts.
If you love our reporting, choose DodgerBlue.com as a preferred source on Google.

item.title: [dailybulletin.com] Analysis: Dodgers’ NLCS defeat raises questions about team’s aging core
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The past two years, the Dodgers’ season ended with parades and calls to “Run it back” for the next season.
After their four-game sweep in the National League Championship Series at the hands of a younger, hungrier Milwaukee Brewers team ended the dream of a ‘three-peat,’ how realistic is it to head into 2027 with the same core – the oldest position player group in MLB for the past four years?
“That’s not my job. I play first base,” said Freddie Freeman, at 37 the oldest returning player on the Dodgers’ roster (infielder Miguel Rojas announced his retirement and relief pitcher Blake Treinen, who suffered a shoulder injury late in the season, is a free agent).
“We’ve got a great group of guys. We’ve accomplished a lot of things. We came up short in these four days. But we’ll see where the wind blows this offseason, what happens, what it looks like, what baseball looks like.”
The winds of change could be coming. As Freeman alluded to, the anticipated showdown between MLB’s owners and the players’ union over the next Collective Bargaining Agreement could force the biggest changes in the Dodgers’ future. If the owners are able to get the salary cap or other payroll restrictions they are aiming for, the Dodgers might be forced to change their roster by shedding payroll.
Also looming over the team’s future are the ongoing legal and financial difficulties surrounding principal owner Mark Walter that threaten to eat into the Dodgers’ enormous financial advantages.
Threatening the franchise’s plans to keep its “Golden Era” going more directly, though, is the aging roster. The Brewers certainly made the Dodgers look old in the four-game NLCS sweep.
“I don’t know what you can really say to that. That’s just people’s opinions of what that is,” Freeman said before Game 4. “We do know we have an older team. That doesn’t mean we’re old and we’re playing bad because we’re old. We’re just not playing that great, in my mind.
“But that’s people’s opinions. I can’t change your opinion because we are, in this game, a little bit older than everybody else. I don’t feel old.”
Nonetheless, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman acknowledged awareness – if not overt concern – about the aging core on the team’s roster.
“Yeah, we’ve talked about this a lot,” Friedman said before the start of the NLCS. “With where we are in the success cycle, the success we have had, we have done the opposite of being flippant about it. ‘Oh, it’s great that we won. Now we can put our feet up.’ For us, it’s about pressing the advantage we have right now.
“We have a very talented core, and while a good number of them are getting up there in years, the experience, the way they prepare, the way they play the game, we feel like is a real competitive advantage. So we’ve been aggressive to supplement around that group, all the while pouring ourselves into our next wave.”
The Dodgers’ farm system is indeed as strong as any in MLB. They subtracted two Top 100 prospects (outfielder Zyhir Hope and right-hander River Ryan) in order to trade for pitcher Tarik Skubal in August and still have five more led by outfielder Josue De Paula.
De Paula made the jump from Double-A to the majors in September and showed his readiness in that brief audition. The Dodgers will have to make room for him in their 2027 plan.
That won’t be easy and it’s difficult to see how the Dodgers can get younger in 2027 other than around the margins where Kiké Hernandez acknowledged Game 4 of the NLCS might be his last with the Dodgers and Rojas made it clear, talking to the team after the game and saying he was retiring. He is expected to stay with the organization in some capacity, likely in player development.
“This is it as a player. That was my last game playing. That was the last time I put these cleats on and this uniform on as a player,” Rojas said, still in full uniform long after the game ended Thursday night. “From now on, I’m going to start thinking about what’s going to happen in my life as a baseball person other than being a player. I want to start my career on the other side of this business, and I’m looking forward to doing it here with the Los Angeles Dodgers as well.
“I’m ready to move on and start the next chapter of my career.”
Hernandez isn’t ready to stop playing. But he knows it might not be in Los Angeles next year.
“I mean, I love this place. I’ve played for three other teams, but every time I look at my career I kind of obviously go back to this place,” the 35-year-old Hernandez said. “I feel like I have a lot left. … I would love to be back. I would love to have one more try, trying to win another one. But I don’t really know what’s going to happen. I hope I’m back, and if I’m not I hope that I get to play for a winning team.”
Seven other Dodgers will become free agents this winter, most prominently bullpen stalwarts Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips and Skubal. Four others – Freeman, outfielder Teoscar Hernandez, third baseman Max Muncy and utility player Hyeseong Kim – are entering the final year of their contracts in 2027, though all but Freeman have club options for 2028.
If the Dodgers are going to change things by their own hand (as opposed to CBA mandate), Teoscar Hernandez clearly has a target on his back as the most likely Dodger to be traded this winter, clearing left field for De Paula. But the Dodgers have largely painted themselves into a corner with this roster. Freeman, shortstop Mookie Betts, catcher Will Smith, center fielder Andy Pages, right fielder Kyle Tucker, two-way star Shohei Ohtani and Muncy, each a year older, are all likely to be in the starting lineup on Opening Day 2027 – whenever that might be.
“I have no idea,” Muncy said of the potential for changes before next season. “That’s for people above me to make those decisions and it’s for me to show up next year, ready to go with whatever group we’ve got. There will come a time when we think about next year. But that’s not at this moment.”
Showing up at Camelback Ranch next spring with the same core is not necessarily a bad thing. Even with only minimal changes, the Dodgers will enter 2027 as the favorites in the National League West once again and a 15th consecutive postseason berth would bring another chance to win the “crapshoot” October has become.
But it also brings this Dodger core closer to “the cliff” Friedman has talked about avoiding.
“It’s tricky because you have to find the right balance,” he said. “It’s hard to transition young players onto your roster. It’s a hard adjustment from Triple-A to the major-league level. We’ve done it some over the years. Some guys we haven’t had the patience long enough to kind of see it through (perhaps an allusion to infielder Miguel Vargas, now an All-Star for the Chicago White Sox).
“That’s the challenge we have with the expectations we have. So we have to be mindful of having a really high standard but also transitioning some of our young players. We’ve seen it some, Andy Pages is featured prominently for us, Will Smith, Alex Freeland got a lot of opportunities this year. Dalton Rushing was a big part when Will missed time. And then late in the year we saw with Josue De Paula.
“We’ve got a lot of guys coming after that as well. So for us it’s about almost having a split personality – to do everything we can to maximize our chances of winning with our major-league roster, and the other side of our personality is pouring ourselves into doing everything we can to have as much talent coming, and we feel really good about that part as well.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — After their earliest postseason exit in three years, the Los Angeles Dodgers head into the offseason facing uncertainty over next year.
Shohei Ohtani was dogged by injuries to his left knee and right biceps over the second half and into the playoffs that rendered him ineffective at the plate. The two-way superstar also didn't pitch after the All-Star break.
Whether Ohtani needs offseason surgery remains to be seen, although he acknowledged it's possible after Thursday's loss to the Brewers that completed Milwaukee's sweep of the NL Championship Series. If he does, would the recovery bleed into the start of next season?
A potential MLB lockout is looming with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on Dec. 1. Team owners have proposed a salary cap — something the sport has never had — and the players' union has adamantly rejected the idea.
A work stoppage would give Ohtani extra time to heal, although during such time the Dodgers would be cut off from communicating with any player, leaving Ohtani to rehab either from possible surgery or from his injuries on his own.
Communication between Ohtani and the team on his health during the season was “awesome,” Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations, said last month, but he added: “The fully sharing exactly how he's feeling, maybe not so awesome.”
Ohtani said he plans to resume pitching next year, when he'll turn 33 in July. He's already had two Tommy John surgeries.
“What he’s doing is unprecedented, and it takes a real toll,” Friedman said. “And as you get older, I think us just being very dialed is going to be really important.”
Roster turnover is likely, even without big changes in MLB spending rules
The Dodgers had baseball's second-highest opening day payroll this year at $323.3 million, behind the New York Mets at $358.4 million. If a salary cap were to be imposed, the Dodgers' spending would be constrained when play resumes.
Some of the roster could look different next year, too, with nine players set to become free agents after the World Series, led by two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, who is expected to command a huge deal.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal from Detroit just before the trade deadline in August. The left-hander was 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts in 10 regular-season games for his new team. In the postseason, he was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA and 14 Ks. Skubal didn't want to discuss his future Thursday, although he expressed enthusiasm for the organization, his teammates and the fans.
Advertisement
Other impending free agents are infielder Miguel Rojas, utility player Kiké Hernández, and relievers Kris Bubic, Brusdar Graterol, Eric Lauer, Evan Phillips, Blake Treinen and Alex Vesia.
As expected, Rojas announced his retirement Thursday, saying, “This is it, guys. That was my last game played.” He'll still be around, though, to work in a player development role.
Dodgers add a bit of youth with De Paula
The Dodgers got a glimpse of the future when they promoted Josue De Paula directly from Double-A to the majors in September. His energy and at-bats at designated hitter during Ohtani's stint on the injured list made an impression, and the 21-year-old was added to the postseason roster as a pinch-hitter.
The team will look to De Paula to further improve as an outfielder in 2027, although finding playing time for him will be challenging given the trio of veteran starters: Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker. De Paula is also blocked at DH by Ohtani.
“I think the experience he got being up here and watching what our guys do on a daily basis just helped connect some dots for him,” Friedman said. “And so, physically, he is capable of being a good corner outfielder, and we’re going to continue to tap into that.”
Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Ohtani, Tucker, Max Muncy and Will Smith will remain the Dodgers' veteran core. But some supporting players could be offloaded, like Kiké Hernández. Playing on a one-year deal, the 35-year-old was limited to 41 games while recovering from injuries and he didn't provide his usual postseason pop.
Manager Dave Roberts refused to blame an aging lineup for getting swept by the Brewers, whose 103 regular-season wins were three more than the Dodgers.
“We got beat,” he said. “There’s no because we’re too old or whatever. Every facet of the game, if you kind of unpack it, we were bested.”
There's drama off the field, too.
Owner Mark Walter was noticeably absent from the team's playoff games. He is facing multiple federal investigations into his business empire for possible financial improprieties involving insurance companies he controls. Walter has denied any wrongdoing. Since August, he sold his controlling interest in the Los Angeles Lakers and last month he unloaded his share in Chelsea of the Premier League.
___

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] As Dodgers grapple with the end of a dynasty, questions abound for Shohei Ohtani, free agency and the coming labor fight
item.dc:creator: Jake Mintz
item.description: LOS ANGELES — In the end, the unfamiliarity outshined the shock. The defeated 2026 Los Angeles Dodgers, many of them back-to-back champs, hadn't been forced to face this uncomfortable silence in a while. A four-game drubbing courtesy of the Milwaukee Brewers in a stunningly comprehensive NLCS sweep cast onto the most expensive team ever assembled a very foreign feeling: failure.
