item.content:encoded:
Best laid plans went awry very early in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series, the sloppiest and wildest game of the Dodgers postseason to date. In a game with four lead changes and two ties, the Dodgers couldn’t get a big hit to save their life, while William Contreras had three different run-scoring hits in the Brewers’ 7-4 win at American Family Field on Monday afternoon in Milwaukee.
The Dodgers head home to Los Angeles down two games to none, with their largest series deficit since the 2023 NLDS.
Chaos to start
It took until the 23rd half-inning of the series for one of these teams to score more than once in a frame, but it wasn’t for lack of trying. Both Jacob Misiorowski and Tarik Skubal labored in big innings in Game 1, but limited the damage to just one run in the rallies.
After single runs for both teams in the first inning, Yoshinobu Yamamoto ran into trouble. David Hamilton singled and stole second base. Brice Turang, who battled back from an 0-2 count and an unchallenged potential third-strike ball call for a double to score in the first inning, worked his way back from an 0-2 count again to walk in the third.
With two outs and two on, first baseman Jake Bauers fouled off six full-count pitches before earning a walk to load the bases.
“Yamamoto — it’s such a big pitch mix,” Bauers said during his media availability before the game. “There’s a lot that you have to try and deal with, and I think you can fall into the trap of trying to guess along with him.”
It took only two more pitches for Yamamoto to hang a curveball to Christian Yelich — in easily the worst of his 14 major league seasons — who singled home two to turn a Dodgers lead into a Dodgers deficit. It also ended Yamamoto’s day, stunningly after needing 75 pitches to get only eight outs, the shortest of his 11 postseason start with the Dodgers.
The dozen pitches to Bauers were the most in any single plate appearance in Yamamoto’s three years in the majors, the entire battle taking seven minutes, 15 seconds per the Fox broadcast.
Only way the Dodgers scored
Brewers starter Logan Henderson allowed only three hits, one of them a ball booted by shortstop Cooper Pratt. Henderson also walked two, but it was three errant throws that proved his undoing. His wild pitch in the first inning put Mookie Betts on third base directly before scoring on a sacrifice fly.
Henderson in the third inning with runners on the corners threw wildly on a pickoff attempt of Betts at first base, allowing Tommy Edman to score from third base. After Kyle Tucker doubled to lead off the fifth inning, Henderson had another throwing error when Edman tried to sacrifice, not only scoring Tucker but putting Edman on second base. He would later score on another sacrifice fly, on a play so close at the plate it required replay review to confirm.
Getting the big hits, or not
Contreras, the Brewers three-time All-Star catcher, singled home a run off Yamamoto in the first inning to tie the game, homered off left-hander Kris Bubic in the fifth inning to tie the game, then singled home a run off Brock Stewart in the sixth to give the Brewers the lead.
It was the third multi-hit game in these playoffs for Contreras, who has three home runs this October.
The Dodgers’ three-time All-Star catcher, Will Smith, was dropped to fifth in the batting order on Monday and was hitless in four at-bats. Smith has one single in 23 at-bats this postseason, with eight strikeouts.
“Obviously want the results to be a little better, but at the end of the day, it’s [six] games at the plate,” Smith told reporters in Milwaukee on Monday before Game 2. “No panic from me. So I’ll be fine.”
Smith isn’t alone in struggles at the plate.
Shohei Ohtani, still batting fourth, was hitless in four at-bats with two strikeouts in Game 2, and has three singles in 19 at-bats plus three walks this postseason.
The Brewers tacked on insurance runs in the eighth inning off Edgardo Henriquez and Justin Wrobleski with three singles and a walk. That put the Brewers up 7-4, the first time either team led by more than one run in this series.
Game 2 of the NLCS was just the second of 27 games this postseason in which both teams scored at least four runs.
Against Henderson the Dodgers were hitless in all of four total at-bats with runners in scoring position, dropping them to 2-for-26 with runners in scoring position this postseason. But once he left with no outs in the fifth inning, the Brewers bullpen completely shut things down the rest of the way.
Dustin May, JoJo Romero, Abner Uribe, and Aaron Ashby faced 15 batters and retired them all. Ashby pitched in multiple innings for a second straight day, this time earning the save.
The Dodgers now face a major uphill battle once they get back home.
NLCS Game 2 particulars
Home run: William Contreras (3)
WP — JoJo Romero (1-1): 1 IP 2 strikeouts
LP — Brock Stewart (0-1): 2/3 IP, 2 hits, 1 run, 1 walk, 1 strikeout
Sv — Aaron Ashby (1): 1 2/3 IP, 2 strikeouts
Up next
The NLCS moves location to Los Angeles beginning with Game 3 on Wednesday evening (5 p.m., FS1). Blake Snell probably starts for the Dodgers, though Dave Roberts earlier Monday wasn’t willing to confirm their plans just yet. Left-hander Robert Gasser starts on the mound for the Brewers.

item.title: [Reviewing the Brew] Dave Roberts’ exposed Game 1 strategy reveals key NLCS matchup for Brewers
item.dc:creator: Owen Jonas

Powered by excellent infield defense, which produced three ground-ball double plays, an incredible swing from Brice Turang that led to a game-tying home run off Tarik Skubal, and another dominant performance from their bullpen, Pat Murphy's squad built a key 1-0 series lead in their quest to knock off the reigning back-to-back World Series champs. After Turang's gam
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers set the series tone on Sunday night with a narrow victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the NLCS. Powered by excellent infield defense, which produced three ground-ball double plays, an incredible swing from Brice Turang that led to a game-tying home run off Tarik Skubal, and another dominant performance from their bullpen, Pat Murphy's squad built a key 1-0 series lead in their quest to knock off the reigning back-to-back World Series champs.
After Turang's game-tying solo shot in the fourth, the Brewers took the lead in the bottom of the fifth thanks to an RBI single from rookie right fielder Luis Lara. The Brewers maintained that narrow one-run lead through the final four innings of the series opener, but they certainly had opportunities to add on to their run total.
Milwaukee's best scoring opportunity came in the bottom of the eighth inning. Jackson Chourio led off the inning with a single to right field off right-handed reliever Evan Phillips. After the leadoff hit, Dodgers manager turned to southpaw Tanner Scott to face Brice Turang, who promptly laid down a sacrifice bunt to advance Chourio to second base, setting up an RBI opportunity for William Contreras.
However, with the left-handed Scott on the mound, Roberts elected to intentionally walk Contreras, setting up a tough left-on-left matchup for Jake Bauers. Scott struck out Bauers on six pitches, which brought lefty-crusher Andrew Vaughn to the plate. Once again, Roberts elected to intentionally walk the righty to set up a left-on-left matchup with Garrett Mitchell. In doing so, however, Roberts moved a key insurance run to third base, where a passed ball or wild pitch would have given the Brewers a two-run lead, and a single would have given them a three-run advantage.
It was undoubtedly a risk for Roberts and the Dodgers -- loading the bases for Mitchell -- but one that paid off on Sunday night. However, in doing so, Roberts exposed a strategy he may use throughout the remainder of the series: prioritizing matchups between his left-handed relievers and the Brewers' left-handed hitters. Such a strategy means the Brewers lefties will have to find ways to produce against Los Angeles' tough bullpen southpaws throughout the series.
The pressure is on the Brewers' left-handed hitters to produce against Dodgers' tough lefty relievers
Left-on-left matchups are something the Brewers are bound to see a lot of throughout the NLCS. From starters Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell to a quartet of lefty relievers in Alex Vesia, Tanner Scott, Kris Bubic, and Justin Wrobleski, Milwaukee can expect to see plenty of southpaws throughout their rematch with the Dodgers.
Clearly, based on last night's strategy, Roberts is going to prioritize matching those lefties up with the Brewers' left-handed hitters by any means necessary. That means there will likely be situations, like last night, where Bauers, Mitchell, Brice Turang, and Christian Yelich will be asked to produce against a same-side pitcher. Concerningly for the Brewers, of that group only Bauers (.901 OPS vs. LHP) had an OPS better than .668 against left-handed pitching during the regular season.
Bauers commented on his improved success against left-handed pitching this year during his pre-game press conference on Monday morning, saying, "A lot of it just has to do with getting the opportunity to see them more often, and then I think I've really focused on developing an approach that gives me the best chance."
On the topic of opportunities, Bauers set a new career-high with 160 plate appearances against left-handed pitchers this year, and already that practice against lefties is coming in handy in the NLCS. Bauers acknowledged the difficult southpaws on the Dodgers' NLCS roster, saying, "Some of these guys, obviously it's not easy, whether it be high arm slot coming from behind you or someone throwing from the side," but in four at-bats in Game 1 last night, all of which came against left-handed pitchers, Bauers went 1-for-3 with a walk and a hard-hit single. Pair that with Turang's impressive blast off Skubal, and the Brewers' left-handers are off to a strong start against same-side pitchers in the NLCS.
Assuming Roberts continues to prioritize these matchups, even if it means intentionally putting runners on base, the pressure will be on Bauers, Turang, and the rest of the Brewers' lefties to continue putting together strong at-bats in these situations. If they can find success against southpaws early in the series, it will certainly complicate Roberts' pitching plan going forward.

item.title: [New York Post] Brewers manager on Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal: ‘I just want to step on his throat’
item.dc:creator: Valentina Martinez
item.description: Brewers manager Pat Murphy made his intentions for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series clear. “I just want to step on his throat,” Murphy said of Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal. “I mean that respectfully.” The Brewers lineup will be looking to exploit any mistakes from Skubal in Sunday’s game at American Family Field. item.content:encoded:
Brewers manager Pat Murphy made his intentions for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series clear.
“I just want to step on his throat,” Murphy said of Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal.
“I mean that respectfully.”
The Brewers lineup will be looking to exploit any mistakes from Skubal in Sunday’s game at American Family Field. A few months ago, Skubal wasn’t even donning Dodger blue.
The two-time Cy Young winner was highly-coveted at the trade deadline and it was the back-to-back World Series champions who managed to land Skubal in a blockbuster trade with the Tigers. Since his arrival to LA, Skubal is sporting a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts across 61 innings pitched.
Now, the left-hander has been given the honor of starting NLCS Game 1 for the Dodgers.
It won’t be an easy feat as Skubal will have to fend off a Brewers lineup that is one of the best offenses in baseball. As Murphy hopes, Milwaukee looks to suffocate Skubal on the mound with their quality at-bats and small ball fundamentals.
Opposite Skubal is National League Cy Young candidate Jacob Misiorowski, who is bound to give the Dodgers lineup some trouble.
The matchup will be the Dodgers’ biggest test of October thus far and the competition will be much, much tougher than it was in 2025, when LA swept the Brewers in four games in the NLCS.
Sunday starts with the Dodgers’ crown jewel of the trade deadline — Skubal.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Pat Murphy sends warning to Tarik Skubal before NLCS Game 1 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers are getting ready to take on the Los Angeles Dodgers, in the National League Championship Series. Brewers manager Pat Murphy is sending a message to Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal, before Game 1.
That message is a powerful one.
"I want to step on his throat," Murphy said, per WFRV-TV in Wisconsin.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The Dodgers and Brewers play Game 1 on Sunday night. Milwaukee's players are ready to go.
"Coming into the postseason, you had a feeling you were going to have to go through L.A.," Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich said, per MLB.com. "They're back-to-back champs, and they're a great team. We have a lot of respect for those guys.
"At the same time, we feel like we can play with anybody when we play our game. When we play our brand of baseball, when we play clean and execute, we're a really hard team to beat. We're going to go in there and grind."
It will be a tough challenge for the Brewers against Skubal. Skubal famously was traded to Los Angeles this season from the Detroit Tigers, ahead of the MLB trade deadline.
"Skubal showed exactly why the Dodgers swung big to acquire him from the Tigers ahead of the Trade Deadline in his NLDS Game 1 start, when he struck out seven across six innings of one-run ball against the Braves. Now, he will take the hill as L.A. begins the next stage of its title defense," MLB.com added.
The Brewers had an outstanding season in the National League. The team won the NL Central, and won 103 games. Milwaukee has done just about everything the last few years but make a World Series.
That is because the Dodgers have always stood in the way. Los Angeles is looking for their third consecutive World Series title this season.
Time will tell if this is finally the year that the Brewers break through that glass ceiling.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Milwaukee Brewers Manager Takes Shot at Tarik Skubal Before NLCS Game One
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series. Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski. Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way. More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Ya
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series.
Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski.
Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way.
More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Yankees with 2-Word Message
Pat Murphy Takes Jab At Tarik Skubal
There’s no doubt that Tarik Skubal is a very stingy pitcher, and it’s very hard to string together success against him, especially in the playoffs.
Skubal has rounded into postseason form over his last handful of starts (Which included a strong Game 1 start against the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS), and looks to be at his peak at the right time.
Per @DodgersNation, Pat Murphy said this about how to beat Skubal:
“Step on his throat… Respectfully.”
“I mean that respectfully because I really like Tarik. My brain can’t go any place else. Go to work, that’s the only mentality I can have.”
It’s a pretty bizarre statement to make before facing a pitcher, but it shows how intense Murphy is and how fired up he is for this matchup.
More MLB on Heavy: Pat Murphy Sounds Off On Tarik Skubal Before Dodgers-Brewers NLCS
Dodgers Set for Battle In NLCS with Brewers
The Milwaukee Brewers are clearly coming into this NLCS with a bit of an edge in terms of being fired up for the matchup.
That’s not to say that the Dodgers aren’t amped up, because they very much are, but after LA swept the Brewers in the 2025 NLCS, it’s hard to think that the Brewers haven’t been thinking about that all year, and in terms of regular-season wins, Milwaukee had an even better campaign in 2026.
However, this Dodgers team is absolutely battle-tested, and they are set up perfectly for another World Series run.
Having Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitching games one and two, and once the series shifts to LA after two games, will allow some comfort for starters Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to pitch at home, which might be a huge boost in the series for the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Kyle Tucker Decision Before NLCS Game 1

item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy has one thing on his mind as his team faces Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Tarik Skubal in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday.
"I just want to step on his throat," Murphy told reporters. He added, "I mean that respectfully, because I really like Tarik, but I just want to beat him."
The Brewers were unable to land Skubal at the trade deadline despite reportedly making a handsome offer to the Detroit Tigers. Instead, the Dodgers acquired the two-time Cy Young winner.
"I just think about, get it done right now," Murphy said. "He's going to be fine. I'm sure he's going to be able to feed his family and be a great dad. He can lose tonight and be fine."
Skubal starts Game 1 of the NLCS opposite Jacob Misiorowski for the Brewers.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers released their lineup for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday, and the placement of Kyle Tucker once again drew attention.
Manager Dave Roberts slotted the outfielder eighth in the order despite the presence of right-hander Jacob Misiorowski on the mound for Milwaukee, a matchup that might otherwise favor a left-handed bat higher in the lineup, via Underdog MLB.
Tucker has occupied that lower spot throughout the postseason, including during the Dodgers’ series against the Atlanta Braves.
The decision keeps him in right field while the top of the order features Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freddie Freeman at first base, Will Smith catching, and Shohei Ohtani as the designated hitter batting cleanup. Teoscar Hernández, Max Muncy, and Andy Pages follow before Tucker, with Enrique Hernández handling second base in place of the unavailable Tommy Edman and Miguel Rojas.
Tarik Skubal, acquired from Detroit at the trade deadline, starts for Los Angeles opposite Misiorowski in the series opener at American Family Field.
The arrangement reflects a broader pattern for Tucker in his first season with the Dodgers. After signing a four-year, $240 million contract in free agency, choosing the defending champions over longer offers elsewhere, he posted a .233 batting average with 17 home runs and 70 RBIs across 154 regular-season games.
Those numbers fell short of the production many expected from a player who had delivered multiple 30-home-run seasons earlier in his career. Roberts and the front office have nonetheless kept him in the everyday mix, banking on the October performance that motivated the signing in the first place.
Tucker has shown signs of that form since early September and carried it into the Division Series. He went 5-for-15 with a home run, two RBIs, and two stolen bases against Atlanta, batting .333 in limited action.
Those at-bats included a two-run homer in the series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the Dodgers seeking a third consecutive World Series appearance, the NLCS against a Brewers club that won 103 games offers the clearest stage yet for the 29-year-old to justify the investment.
A productive stretch against Milwaukee’s pitching staff would quiet questions about his regular-season output and reinforce the club’s bet that his best baseball remains ahead.
For now, the eighth spot keeps Tucker in the lineup without disrupting the balance Roberts has settled on for the series.
Both clubs enter the matchup after efficient Division Series victories, and the early pitching duel between Skubal and Misiorowski sets a high bar for the hitters behind them.
Tucker’s ability to contribute from the lower third of the order will factor into whether Los Angeles can seize an early advantage on the road.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Tarik Skubal Eager for the "Privilege" of More Postseason Pressure
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI — Tarik Skubal feels healthy, fresh and ready to take the ball for the Dodgers in Sunday’s NLCS opener. Speaking at Saturday’s workout in Milwaukee, he praised the Brewers’ lineup and the pitcher he will face, Jacob Misiorowski. He also explained the easygoing start-day routine that has caught his teammates’ attention. For Skubal, being himself and keeping the task simple are part of getting ready for a game like this. item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE, WI — Tarik Skubal feels healthy, fresh and ready to take the ball for the Dodgers in Sunday’s NLCS opener. Speaking at Saturday’s workout in Milwaukee, he praised the Brewers’ lineup and the pitcher he will face, Jacob Misiorowski. He also explained the easygoing start-day routine that has caught his teammates’ attention. For Skubal, being himself and keeping the task simple are part of getting ready for a game like this.
Milwaukee makes pitchers earn it
Skubal sees a Brewers team that can win in several ways, with hitters who make pitchers work throughout the order.
“First off, it’s a very talented roster. I think they do a lot of things really well,” he said. “They pitch, they play defense, they run the bases, they hit with runners in scoring position. They control the zone really well. Their walk percentage is up there at the top of the big leagues, I think, one through nine. And they don’t strike out a lot.”
“It’s a really good baseball team. They play the game the right way. I’ve got a lot of respect for the guys over there, and obviously the manager, Murph. I’m a big fan of his.”
On the mound, Skubal knows he will have to get ahead and earn outs in the strike zone.
“You’ve got to match it when you’re on the mound. Do everything you can to get ahead and understand they’re not going to chase,” he said. “Sometimes you’ve got to beat them in the zone. I think it’s going to be a fun matchup.”
Finding his own routine
Max Muncy and Dave Roberts have both spoken about how easy Skubal is to talk to on the day he pitches. Earlier in his career, he tried following the example of older starters.
“You come up and see all the older guys and the way they go about things. Almost always, they all have headphones in. They don’t really talk to anybody, and everybody stays out of their way,” Skubal said. “You naturally think, ‘Okay, that’s what big leaguers do. This is what I’m going to do.’”
“I did that early in my career, and I found it to be pretty exhausting. I found myself mentally exhausted in the second or third innings of games. I’m like, ‘Why am I tired? I should be ready to go today.’”
An injury in 2022 gave him time to rethink that approach.
“When I got hurt in ’22, I decided enough is enough. I’m caring way too much about all the little things that don’t really matter and don’t really impact the game of baseball,” he said. “Making sure the music is the right setting, making sure it’s the right songs at the right times. You’re caring about all the wrong things, I think.”
“For me, it was more mentally freeing to take my headphones off and be who I am and interact with guys. As it gets closer to game time, you get ready to go, and you’re going to go out there and compete.”
“I want to be myself, and then I’ll lock in as the game gets closer.”
A clubhouse that welcomed him
Skubal said the Dodgers encouraged him to bring that same approach when he joined the club.
“They have a culture where they want guys to be who they are. Be your authentic self, and they’re going to appreciate you for whatever that is,” he said. “Every guy’s different. We’re all humans at the end of the day, and we all tick differently. They wanted me to be me. That was the message early on.”
Getting to know his teammates took time, along with learning how each of them works.
“That’s something I also value, how to get everybody else going and marching in one direction,” he said. “Understanding how to communicate, that stuff takes time.”
“The clubhouse is great. Obviously, a veteran group, but at the same time very welcoming to who I am. We both have the same goal in mind, and that’s to win a World Series. That starts with Game 1 tomorrow.”
Respect for Misiorowski
Skubal enjoys studying pitching, and Misiorowski has given him plenty to watch. Beyond the velocity, he admires the right-hander’s ability to throw strikes.
“His ability to command pitches at that velocity consistently, he consistently gets ahead,” Skubal said. “Obviously, the velocity is what it is, and the stuff and the shapes are what they are. But I think his walk percentage and walks per nine are about as impressive as anything he does.”
“He forces teams to beat him. That’s the mark of a really good starting pitcher, a guy who’s going to force lineups to beat you. He does all those things.”
“As a fan of the game, I’m a fan as much as I’m a player, it’s fun to watch him pitch. Tomorrow is probably going to be a different story, but what he does is very impressive.”
“The pressure is a privilege”
The expectations around the Dodgers suit Skubal’s own goals.
“The pressure surrounding the Dodgers, I think it’s all a privilege,” he said. “As an athlete, this is what you want to be in. You want to have an expectation to win. I have those same expectations as a player.”
“Keeping the game the game, going out there and competing and doing what I can to put my team in a position to win, I think, is important. In bigger moments, simplify. Be who you are and leave it all out on the field.”
“You can live with whatever result happens as long as you gave it everything you had out there. That’s what I ask of myself every time out.”
Asked about his workload and how he feels heading into this start, Skubal gave an encouraging report.
“I feel good right now; I feel fresh. I feel healthy. That’s all you can ask for at this time of year,” he said. “The body feels good. I feel like the ball’s coming out really well, and I’m able to execute pitches.”
He wants to stay on the mound, while trusting Roberts and the relievers when it is time to hand over the ball.
“You trust the manager, trust the plan they have, trust the guys in the bullpen,” Skubal said. “The bullpen we have here is also very talented and can give us an advantage later in the game. You’ve got to trust that stuff and also trust where the game is, the situation.”
“I’m excited to go.”

item.content:encoded:
To the surprise of absolutely no one, the Dodgers and Braves are headed back to the NLCS. The entire LCS slate turned out (almost) the way everyone expected, as the three teams with the best regular season records in baseball have advanced to fight for their league's pennants, with the Guardians (ugh) playing spoiler on the American League side.
Tarik Skubal will get the ball for Game 1 of the NLCS against Jacob Misiorowski and a Brewers team that was rumored to be in on Skubal's trade market at the deadline. The Dodgers just rolled through their NLDS against the Braves, who were also in on the Skubal chase.
The Tigers seemed enamored by the package the Dodgers had to offer, but that doesn't mean that Scott Harris didn't negotiate with other teams. He was reportedly asking for a king's ransom, which only Andrew Friedman and LA were willing to give up for a rental.
According to Peter Abraham of the Boston Globe, the Braves were unwilling to part with reliever and potential closer-in-the-making Didier Fuentes, who posted a 2.45 ERA in 73 1/3 innings and a 3.86 ERA this postseason. In Atlanta's only win of the NLDS, he pitched an admirable 3 2/3-inning appearance and only gave up one run — a Max Muncy home run down to LA's last strike.
Braves were reportedly unwilling to give up Didier Fuentes in Tarik Skubal trade talks with Tigers
Fuentes was included in our Braves-Tigers trade proposal for Skubal alongside starter JR Ritchie and outfield prospect Patrick Clohisy. In an ideal world, that is how the trade would've shaken out: a controllable starter, a controllable backend bullpen arm, and a controllable outfielder.
The Dodgers were willing to give up two out of three in starter River Ryan and outfielder Zyhir Hope (and the jury will remain out on Brady Smith). The Tigers knew that none would be available to help them immediately, but the pedigree was evidently too hard to pass up.
Atlanta including Fuentes would've given them a leg up. Here was a controllable bullpen arm who's being primed for a long-term future as a closer, who could've slotted into the Tigers' awful bullpen immediately and maybe helped them thread the needle far more effectively than they actually did.
The teams that chose to back out of the Skubal bidding, including the Braves and Brewers, will have all offseason to ponder whether or not they should've just buckled down and overpaid for a rental — because it's working out pretty swimmingly for the Dodgers.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Tarik Skubal raves about Jacob Misiorowski, but Brewers starter passes
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: There is added intrigue with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers squaring off in the National League Championship Series for a second year in a row thanks to the pitching matchup of Tarik Skubal and Jacob Misiorowski. item.content:encoded:
There is added intrigue with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers squaring off in the National League Championship Series for a second year in a row thanks to the pitching matchup of Tarik Skubal and Jacob Misiorowski.
Skubal is the reigning two-time American League Cy Young Award winner, and Misiorowski is the presumed NL winner for 2026. Misiorowski downplayed starting opposite Skubal, but the left-hander was more than willing to heap praise on his counterpart.
“He’s very impressive. His ability to command pitches at that velocity consistently, consistently gets ahead,” Skubal began. “I think what stands out with him is obviously the velocity is what it is, and the stuff and the shapes are what they are, but I think his walk percentage and walk per nine is about as impressive as what he does.
“He doesn’t walk anybody. He forces teams to beat him. He doesn’t really beat himself too many times when he’s out there. I think that’s the mark of a really good starting pitcher is a guy that’s not going to beat themselves, going to force lineups to beat you.
“He does all those things. As a fan of the game — I’m a fan as much as I’m a player — it’s fun to watch him pitch. Now, tomorrow is probably going to be a different story, but yeah, what he does is very impressive.”
Comparatively, Misiorowski chose to highlight his focus being on facing the Dodgers, similar to when he’s previously been asked about starting in the same game as Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes.
“Like I said countless times before when I face Skenes or any guy like that, I’m not really looking at them. I’m looking at the lineup more than him,” Misiorowski explained.
“For me personally, it doesn’t really mean that much to face a guy like that. Obviously it’s cool. The dude’s insane. But I’m just hoping that these guys can do their job and handle business with him and let me do my thing and try to get that side taken care of.”
Skubal heads into a second consecutive Game 1 start with the Dodgers having gone 5-0 with 1.95 ERA in his last five outings, including the NL Division Series.
Meanwhile, Misiorowski has a career 1.59 ERA and 40.9% strikeout rate in three games (two starts) against the Dodgers, including the postseason.
Jacob Misiorowski respecting Shohei Ohtani
When Misiorowski faced the Dodgers during the regular season, he uncorked multiple fastballs over 100 mph to Shohei Ohtani. And although the Dodgers’ star has been mired in a prolonged slump, the hard-throwing righty is not taking him lightly.
“It’s still October. They’re going to find a way to get a bat on ball and get on base how they can,” Misiorowski said. “You got to still pitch like he’s the best in the world and trust your stuff, and go beat him at his game and do your job.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have an injury update on veteran infielder Miguel Rojas after he left Game 3 of the National League Division Series early after an errant swing caused major back discomfort. Though he didn't appear in the series-clinching Game 4, manager Dave Roberts still seemed hopeful that last season's World Series hero would be back in time for the the NL Champinship Series rematch against the Milwaukee Brewers.
"I just talked to him briefly, he's in good spirits," Roberts said on Saturday. "We're going to talk to him right now, but as far as the flight, I'm expecting him to be a part of it, be on the roster."
In other news, two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal opened up about his love for his new team.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal ahead of the trade deadline after he spent the previous six seasons with the Detroit Tigers. With his impending free agency likely pointing towards a contract worth $400 million or more, Dodgers fans should feel more at ease that the southpaw won't look to leave LA before after his most recent comments.
"It's a great team," Skubal said. “The culture that they have here. The preparation, the expectation to win — I love being a part of it."
Finally, Brewers manager Pat Murphy once again has decided to go with the underdog approach ahead of the NLCS. The 103-win Brewers do not appear to be underdogs purely going by regular season records, (or with possessing home field advantage), but the skipper spoke on different "luxuries" that LA has over Milwaukee.
"I just have the front office to thank for being able to pick up the right guys because those type of guys have filled in and did really nicely for us," Muprhy said. "But we don't have the luxury of maybe you have a guy that hadn't pitched much and he's going to make his debut in August. He's a $30 million two-time Cy Young winner or something like that. We don't have that cushion. So we're more desperate to play every single game."

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Tarik Skubal Defends Clayton Kershaw for Unfair Postseason Narrative
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: There is no doubt that Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw is one of the best pitchers of this generation. The Dodgers southpaw is a surefire Hall of Famer after 18 spectacular seasons on the mound, all in Los Angeles. Kershaw helped catapult the Dodgers to new heights during his tenure, but his postseason struggles were evident. Kershaw is considered one of the greatest regular-season pitchers in baseball history, but the conversation changes when it comes to his October performance. How
item.content:encoded:
There is no doubt that Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw is one of the best pitchers of this generation.
The Dodgers southpaw is a surefire Hall of Famer after 18 spectacular seasons on the mound, all in Los Angeles.
Kershaw helped catapult the Dodgers to new heights during his tenure, but his postseason struggles were evident.
Kershaw is considered one of the greatest regular-season pitchers in baseball history, but the conversation changes when it comes to his October performance.
However, it's not entirely black and white when it comes to Kershaw and October.
Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal recently defended Kershaw against the unfair postseason narrative surrounding him.
“I don’t really buy into that narrative with Kersh, the postseason struggles,” Skubal said.
On the surface, Kershaw's play in the regular season versus October is stark.
His regular-season ERA sits at 2.43, while his postseason ERA sits at 4.30. On top of that, Kershaw has had a number of meltdowns, including the 2023 National League Division Series against the Ariziona Diamondbacks and a 2019 relief appearance against the Washington Nationals.
Those meltdowns disproportionately skew his career postseason ERA over roughly 200 innings.
A ton of factors play into that, including the workload he endured before October. Kershaw made 41 postseason appearances, but four came on short rest, and nine were relief appearances.
“It takes a superhuman to be held to the standard he was being held to, in the biggest of moments,” Skubal said. “I think he was great. He did everything he could for his team. He wore it out there sometimes. Chasing box scores and stuff is kind of unfair to judge guys on, because I’m sure he was pitching through some stuff and grinding through some stuff.
“But he had to do it, because he was Clayton Kershaw.”
How Much Blame Does Clayton Kershaw Deserve for His Playoff Struggles?
The bad often outweighs the good, and that is no exception when it comes to Kershaw.
He had some stellar outings, including Game 2 of the 2016 NL Championship Series against the Chicago Cubs, Game 1 of the 2013 NLDS against the Atlanta Braves and Game 1 of the 2020 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Kershaw certainly deserves some blame; however, managers like Don Mattingly and Dave Roberts occasionally left him out too long, which eventually led to those blow-up innings where he got the blame.
Either way, Skubal — like many other MLB fans and pundits — doesn't buy into the "choker" label that has been unfairly placed on Kershaw.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.dc:creator: JAY COHEN

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — All along, Christian Yelich felt this was going to be part of the road for the Milwaukee Brewers.
It was always going to be the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers — with their consecutive World Series titles and a payroll that casts a long shadow over Yelich and the small-market Brewers.
“We’ve been expecting having to play them in this round since spring training, in the regular season,” Yelich said Saturday. “You kind of just know that’s what’s going to happen.”
The 2026 NL Championship Series is a sequel, with Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers taking on Jackson Chourio and the Brewers. Los Angeles swept Milwaukee in last year's NLCS on the way to the franchise's 26th NL pennant and ninth World Series championship. The Dodgers also eliminated the Brewers in the NLCS in 2018 and the wild-card round in 2020.
Game 1 on Sunday night features a pair of stingy aces. Tarik Skubal goes for Los Angeles after the two-time Cy Young Award winner was acquired in an Aug. 1 trade with Detroit, and Jacob Misiorowski — the front-runner for the NL Cy Young Award — starts for Milwaukee.
The return engagement for the NLCS also shines a light on the competing arguments at the center of MLB's collective bargaining negotiations. Baseball’s five-year labor contract expires Dec. 1, and management is expected to lock out players in a confrontation that could affect the 2027 season.
The Dodgers went 100-62 this season and won the NL West for the fifth straight year after they had an opening-day payroll of $323.6 million, second only to the New York Mets. Milwaukee's opening-day payroll of $125.9 million ranked 20th, and the Brewers set a franchise record with a major league-best 103 wins on the way to their fourth consecutive Central title.
“We’re focused on trying to win, and I think we have for a while,” Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said. “Regardless of what the economics look like, the guys in there believe, and so do I.”
Milwaukee was shut down by Los Angeles in last year's playoffs, hitting .118 while managing just one run in each game in the sweep. Ohtani punctuated the series by swatting three solo homers and striking out 10 over six shutout innings in Game 4.
Ohtani won't pitch this time around because of injuries, and the Japanese slugger went 2 for 13 with four strikeouts in the four-game NL Division Series against Atlanta. But the Dodgers still have a formidable rotation, fronted by Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
“Every night when you play these guys, you know you’re going to face a great pitcher, a Cy Young-caliber pitcher,” Yelich said.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski isn't changing approach even with Shohei Ohtani's slump appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Shohei Ohtani has just one extra base hit in his last 16 games and has not recorded a home run since Aug. 18. Calling the four-time MVP a shell of himself is underselling this shocking slump. He is clearly not 100 percent after battling knee, bicep and neck injuries this year. Milwaukee Brewers superstar Jacob Misiorowski still sees a unicorn, however, and he is not about to underestimate him in the biggest start of his MLB career.
The presumptive NL Cy Young Award winner intends to show Ohtani complete respect when the two face off in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday night.
"It's still October," Misiorowski told reporters, per the Dodger Blue YouTube account. "They're going to find a way to get a bat on ball and get on base how they can, so you got to still pitch like he's the best in the world. Trust your stuff and go beat him at his game and do your job."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The 6-foot-7 right-hander is saying all the right stuff ahead of this NLCS rematch. He remembers what Ohtani did last year. The Japanese juggernaut finished off LA's sweep of the Brewers by mashing three home runs and striking out 10 batters in six scoreless innings pitched. It may be the greatest single-game performance ever.
Yes, he is not pitching this postseason, and yes, his bat is ice-cold, but Shohei Ohtani can still make a massive impact as long as he is in the lineup. Jacob Misiorowski can obviously do the same from the mound.
Following an inconsistent showing versus the San Diego Padres in the NL Division Series — two earned runs in four innings — the 24-year-old aims to squash the two-time reigning World Series champions in American Family Field. Consecutive ho-hum outings is highly unlikely. Misiorowski posted an MLB-best 1.80 ERA, 252 strikeouts and 0.802 WHIP in 174 2/3 innings during the regular season.
The Dodgers are a different kind of beast in the playoffs, but so is he. After a shaky end to his rookie campaign, the 2022 second-round draft pick regrouped and thrived out of the Milwaukee bullpen in the 2026 MLB postseason. He threw 12 magnificent innings that helped launch him into elite status in 2026. Misiorowski's confidence should be at an all-time high entering the NLCS.
But no amount of self-assurance will convince him to shrug off Ohtani. This mega matchup will take place at approximately 8 p.m. ET on Sunday.

item.title: [MLB.com] Dream Skubal-Miz showdown all set for NLCS Game 1

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, while the Brewers announced Saturday that they will have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. Both teams clinched their spot in the NLCS on Thursday, the Brewers with a 3-1 win over the Padres and the Dodgers with a 4-1 win over the Braves.
Misiorowski pitched just once in the series, throwing four innings of two-run ball in Game 1. Similarly, Skubal opened things against the Braves, going six innings with just one run allowed, and did not pitch again. Both should be well-rested.
The most realistic argument against a Skubal-Misiorowski duel lies in October superstar Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the Dodgers righty pitched in Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, meaning he’d start Sunday on just four days’ rest. He will pitch in Game 2 on Monday with a regular recovery that would make more sense.
We’ve seen great pitching in the 2026 postseason thus far and several marquee matchups: Cam Schlittler vs. Payton Tolle; Chris Sale vs. Jesús Luzardo; Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray; Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen; Yamamoto vs. Sale.
But Skubal vs. Misiorowski will take the cake.
After some struggles late in the regular season, Misiorowski pitched behind an opener when he made his postseason debut a year ago, but he was effective in three appearances. He allowed only one run across seven innings in the NLDS against the Cubs, before striking out nine and yielding just one run in five innings against the Dodgers in the NLCS.
But this is not the same Miz in 2026. The flame-throwing 24-year-old finished the regular season with MLB bests in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), WHIP (0.80) and opponents’ batting average (.157). It was more than a breakout -- it was among the greatest pitching seasons in MLB history.
Misiorowski’s four-seam fastball topped out at 104.8 mph and averaged 101.2 mph against the Padres in the NLDS. With the adrenaline that is sure to be present on Sunday, who knows what eye-popping numbers he could put up.
As for Skubal, he won’t win a third consecutive Cy Young. But that won’t take away from the 2.72 ERA he posted in 26 starts, including a 2.61 mark after his blockbuster trade to the Dodgers. Remember, too, that Skubal missed 44 days in the summer after he needed surgery to remove loose bodies in his left elbow. There have been few signs of rust from that recovery.
Skubal’s strong playoff debut with the Dodgers was just more of what we’re used to from the southpaw. He made six postseason starts as a Tiger in 2024 and 2025 with a 2.04 ERA, never going shorter than six innings and allowing more than two runs just once.
The Brewers and Dodgers will already provide appointment viewing throughout the NLCS, a rematch of the 2025 NL pennant battle and a meeting of MLB’s top regular-season teams in 2026. Add in the bout of Misiorowski and Skubal in Game 1, and this series should get off to an awfully hot start.

item.dc:creator: BETH HARRIS
item.description: LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday.
Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-hander struck out seven and walked two.
Yamamoto started Game 3 of the NLDS, and struck out 10 over seven innings. The right-hander allowed one run and four hits to go with one walk.
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell struggled as the Game 2 starter against the Braves, who won 3-2 to tie the best-of-five series 1-1. The Dodgers went on to eliminate the Braves, 3-1.
Roberts said the Dodgers were in discussions about adding a pitcher for the best-of-seven NLCS, which would require them to drop a position player. Rosters are due Sunday morning.
Miguel Rojas exited Game 3 against the Braves during an at-bat with lower back pain. The utility player underwent imaging, which mostly showed prior back issues. He took ground balls and a couple rounds of batting practice at Dodger Stadium on Friday.
Rojas, 37, has said he's leaning toward retiring at the end of the season.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “We still have a flight to get on and see how he comes in tomorrow for the workout there, so there’s nothing definitive.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers legend explains why Tarik Skubal trade means more in MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers already knew Tarik Skubal could change their rotation. Now, a Dodgers legend has explained why the move could matter even more in October. Skubal was brought in from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline for a package that included top prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith. The Dodgers did not make that investment simply to strengthen their regular-season rotation. They wanted another ace for the moments when every game carries significantly more weight. Tha
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers already knew Tarik Skubal could change their rotation. Now, a Dodgers legend has explained why the move could matter even more in October.
Skubal was brought in from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline for a package that included top prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith. The Dodgers did not make that investment simply to strengthen their regular-season rotation. They wanted another ace for the moments when every game carries significantly more weight.
That value was on full display in the National League Division Series.
Tarik Skubal is built for the postseason stage
Skubal started Game 1 against the Atlanta Braves and delivered exactly what Los Angeles hoped to get when it made the trade.
The left-hander allowed one run and two hits over six innings while striking out seven. He also retired 15 consecutive hitters at one point, helping the Dodgers take a 5-3 victory and an early series lead.
The Dodgers eventually finished off Atlanta in four games, advancing to the NL Championship Series.
That is where the importance of the Skubal trade becomes clearer.
Los Angeles already had talented arms, but postseason baseball can expose even the deepest rotation. A starter who can take the ball in Game 1 and immediately settle a series gives a team something that regular-season depth cannot fully measure.
Sep 19, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) reacts after giving up a walk to the San Francisco Giants in the during the second inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Skubal's first season with Los Angeles has backed up that idea. He went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts in 10 regular-season starts for the Dodgers.
Now the stakes are even higher.
The Dodgers will face Milwaukee after the Brewers finished the regular season with an MLB-best 103-59 record. The series is a rematch of last year's NLCS, and Skubal is in line to face Misiorowski in Sunday's opener if both teams follow their expected rotation plans.
That is precisely why Los Angeles surrendered so much prospect capital for Skubal.
The Dodgers did not need another good regular-season pitcher. They needed someone capable of taking the ball when the margin for error disappears.
After his Game 1 performance against Atlanta, Skubal has already shown that the trade can pay off where it matters most. Now he gets another chance to prove it with a trip to the World Series on the line.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers will have time to reset rotation, bullpen, and struggling Shohei Ohtani for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5. By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5.
By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game.
"It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happen. And to be able to win today, get back, reset, have a day off tomorrow, set the rotation, it's huge."
The extra rest means Tarik Skubal likely will be the choice to start against Milwaukee instead of handling a Game 5 against the Braves. Similarly, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow will be well rested for their expected NLCS starts.
Infielder Miguel Rojas may need the extra rest for a sore lower back that kept him out.
Also, Edwin Díaz will have ample time to reset after recording saves on back-to-back days to close out the series against Atlanta. The ninth-inning work showed Díaz is re-established as the closer.
"The team trusts me," Díaz said. "I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it's been amazing. That's why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I'm really happy right now."
Despite those advantages, Roberts is preparing for a tough NLCS as the Dodgers try to move closer to their goal of becoming the first NL team to win three consecutive World Series.
"We've got our work cut out," Roberts said, adding extra rest also will be important for such players as Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
Ohtani was 2 for 13 against Atlanta and hasn't homered since Aug. 18 while dealing with injuries to his right biceps, left knee and neck that have also kept the two-way player off the mound.
"So kind of enjoy this one, get Shohei a couple of days to get back," Roberts said. "Freddie, he had a big series, but, again a couple of days will help him. Give our guys in the 'pen a little reset. So we'll be ready to go Game 1."
Díaz pitched a perfect ninth inning in the clinching win. The on-field celebration was a low-key affair, but Roberts and his players, wearing "Take October" T-shirts and goggles to protect their eyes, soon were drenched with champagne.
The Dodgers made the most of their opportunity to celebrate another postseason series win while maintaining their focus on a third straight World Series championship.
"Our goal is to win the World Series, not this series," Díaz said. "We've got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
"Now we're going back to LA to keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to LA, get working and be ready for Sunday."
Andy Pages' bases-loaded single in the seventh drove in two runs to give the Dodgers a 3-1 lead. Max Muncy added to the lead with a homer in the ninth, his third blast of the postseason.
"Obviously, we have big teams, big series coming up," Pages said. "We're going to face tough teams, so prepare for those moments, but also take advantage of the opportunity of being here and enjoying these moments. And knowing that our ultimate goal is to win the World Series. So focus on that."

item.title: [New York Post] Doctober classic propels Dodgers to NLCS in quest for World Series three-peat
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate. So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches? So what if he was still in the fifth inning? Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances. Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate.
So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches?
So what if he was still in the fifth inning?
Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances.
Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series.
The Dodgers advanced to the NL Championship Series.
Because of Tarik Skubal.
Because of Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
Because of Freddie Freeman.
And because of David Ray Roberts, the manager affectionately known as Doc who has a game or two like this every October.
The victory over the Braves on Wednesday was a Doctober classic.
On a day in which one of his four aces lasted only 4 ⅔ innings, Roberts figured out how to cover 13 outs of the game with a notoriously unpredictable bullpen.
Roberts’ fingerprints were also all over Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning that broke open the game.
When Teoscar Hernandez singled that inning with one out, Braves manager Walt Weiss replaced starting pitcher Tyler Mahle with right-hander Didier Fuentes.
Fuentes forced Max Muncy to ground out, but Hernandez advanced to second base on the play.
Due up was Game 3 hero Kike Hernandez.
Rather than have the right-handed utilityman face Fuentes, Roberts deployed rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch hitter. The left-handed-hitting De Paula drew a walk, at which point he was replaced on the basepaths by Tommy Edman.
Kyle Tucker followed up with another walk to load the bases, at which point Weiss turned to fireballer Robert Suarez to pitch to Pages.
Pages batted .078 in the postseason last year, which resulted in his benching in the World Series. He was 0-for-7 in the first two games of this series, but Roberts stuck with him.
Roberts’ faith was rewarded by the most important hit of Pages’ three-year career, a single to right field that drove in two runs to push the Dodgers in front, 3-1. The runs were the Dodgers’ first of the series that weren’t scored via a home run.
The manager demonstrated an equal level of creativity in directing his bullpen.
Vesia returned for the sixth inning, only to give up a leadoff double to Ozzie Albies. Roberts kept the left-hander in for another batter, the left-handed-hitting Drake Baldwin, who lined out.
Roberts’ next call to the bullpen was for Edgardo Henriquez, who spent the last two weeks of the regular season on the injured list. Henriquez gave up a run in the Dodgers’ Game 2 loss, but not only did Roberts trust him to prevent Albies from scoring, he also had him pitch the seventh inning.
From there, it was simple.
Tanner Scott pitched the eighth inning. With Muncy homering in the ninth inning to increase the lead to 4-1, Edwin Diaz came in to record the last three outs.
The Dodgers moved to within four wins of playing in their third consecutive World Series, and they did it with Shohei Ohtani still missing in action.
Ohtani was 2-for-13 in this series.
“It’s good to know that we can still win games without him doing a whole bunch,” Roberts said. “But he’s going to come to life. It will happen.”
Roberts has squinted extra hard in recent days to find evidence of that.
Here’s the reality: In his last 22 combined games between the regular season and playoffs, Ohtani has no home runs and only one RBI.
That isn’t a slump.
The No. 1 player in the game doesn’t go this long without hitting in the prime of his career without something being seriously wrong with him.
Ohtani spent 15 days last month on the injured list because of a discomfort in his right arm. A couple of days before he was placed on the IL, he said his left knee was also bothering him.
The uncertainty over Ohtani’s capabilities forced Roberts to move him around the lineup.
With Mookie Betts grinding out quality at-bats as the leadoff hitter and Freeman producing enough to solidify his place as the team’s No. 2 hitter, Ohtani was removed from the top of the order.
Against the left-handed Chris Sale in Game 3, Ohtani batted fifth. Against the right-handed Mahle on Wednesday, he batted cleanup.
Ohtani managed to create something out of nothing in the second inning. He drew a walk, then stole second base, prompting Braves catcher Sean Murphy to airmail a throw into center field. Ohtani scampered to third base. When Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubón dropped a popup by Muncy in shallow left field, Ohtani scored to tie the game at 1.
Ohtani didn’t collect any hits Wednesday, but he didn’t have to.
Roberts had the game under control.

item.title: [Rising Apple] Qualifying offer penalty can quickly eliminate NY Mets' Tarik Skubal backup plan
item.dc:creator: Tim Boyle
item.description: I Stand Alone was a 2002 song by the rock band Godsmack featured in the film The Scorpion King. item.content:encoded:
I Stand Alone was a 2002 song by the rock band Godsmack featured in the film The Scorpion King. The song hardly stands alone as their lone hit or even above some of their lesser remembered releases. In MLB free agency, it’s Tarik Skubal who stands alone as the best of the bunch this offseason both from a pitching and hitting perspective. His market will be limited to the Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Mets, and maybe a mystery team thrown in.
Alternatives you ask? They aren’t good, Bob. One of the most realistic is Trevor Rogers. He was someone the Mets tried to trade for at the 2024 deadline only to come up short as he went from the Miami Marlins to the Baltimore Orioles instead. Terrible for Baltimore down the stretch, brilliant in an abbreviated 2025, and more average with signs of excellence in 2026, he’s a guy we should definitely believe fits the model of how David Stearns operates.
Rogers turns 29 this November. For him, coming off of a 10-11, 4.01 ERA season means seeking out an opportunity to maybe have an amazing 2027 and/or 2028 and re-enter free agency still young enough to get one of those fat contracts.
If Trevor Rogers receives a qualifying offer and rejects it, the Mets have to think twice about signing him
The QO was pretty much made for players like Rogers. He had a good, not great year. His 101 ERA+ suggests he was a fraction better than average.
However you want to rate him, it’s a little icky to think about giving up two draft picks to sign him. The Mets will, yet again, lose draft pick compensation for signing a QO rejector. The Mets lost $1 million in international bonus slot money plus their second and fifth highest draft picks last offseason when they inked Bo Bichette. Those same penalties should apply again this offseason if they choose to take the leap.
There are players where draft picks don’t matter. Juan Soto cost the Mets two picks and the international bonus slot money. Nobody argued. Eve Bichette felt worth it in some ways especially with the Mets already gaining a selection when Edwin Diaz departed.
Rogers seems a sure bet to decline the qualifying offer. He can guarantee himself more than what it’s worth and with additional years of control. Some health issues in his career will always have a pitcher in free agency looking for a way to capitalize and protect in case of another injury.
Not as expensive as Skubal yet costly to those of us who still haven’t adjusted baseball salaries for inflation, Rogers will find a way to guarantee himself around $50 million over two years plus additional seasons. He’s the kind of guy you sign for what you believe he will do and not what he has already accomplished. It’s not all that different from Zack Wheeler. During his time with the Mets, he was no ace but very good at times. The Philadelphia Phillies believed in the future enough. Will the Mets do so with Rogers?
Stearns hasn’t been hesitant to give out deals like this with inferior players. Frankie Montas getting a $17 million deal for 2025 plus the player option for 2026 never sat well with fans. Sean Manaea, Clay Holmes, and even Pete Alonso were all signed for short contracts with a player option. Oh, and Bichette, too. Even Soto has a chance to opt out with the creative pushback where the Mets can increase his salary to avoid him leaving.
Rogers is a part of the Plan-B package if the Mets miss on Skubal. Is it satisfactory enough? Plan-B requires one other addition. Rogers has had flashes of being awesome while the overall results have been more “meh.” That has been the M.O. under Stearns and whether we like it or not, he feels destined to become a hot Mets rumor this winter.
The qualifying offer penalty, perhaps, becomes too rich when the team can just as easily pivot to others who won’t have the same punishment following them around. The big irony is that because Skubal was traded mid-season he wouldn't cost the Mets anything more than cash. With Rogers, there's an added cost.

item.content:encoded:
When will Dodgers' Tarik Skubal pitch next in NLDS? Here's the latest update appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently gearing up for Game 3 of their NLDS series against the Atlanta Braves on Tuesday afternoon on the road. The Dodgers are currently tied 1-1 with Atlanta after dropping a frustrating contest in Game 2 at home over the weekend.
The Dodgers won Game 1 of this series thanks in large part to a dominant pitching performance from ace Tarik Skubal, and now, the latest reporting has revealed when Skubal could be on the mound again for Los Angeles.
"Tarik Skubal throwing bullpen session in preparation for his next start…possibly Game 5," reported David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports on X, formerly Twitter.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Of course, if the Dodgers have their way, they'll win the next two games in Atlanta and avoid a Game 5 altogether, in which case Skubal would likely be the starter for Game 1 of the ensuing NLCS.
However, Los Angeles certainly has their work cut out for them in order to make that scenario a reality. Los Angeles' main hitters, headlined by Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani, have largely been dormant so far in this series, with the team mustering just two runs in Sunday's loss to Atlanta despite the Braves running out an all-bullpen lineup.
On Tuesday, Los Angeles will face off against the formidable Chris Sale, who is coming off a long rest after Walt Weiss opted not to rush him back in Game 2 in a gutsy move that ended up paying off.
The Dodgers will certainly want to see their bats come to life in Game 3 to retake control of the series.
Game 3 between the Dodgers and Braves is slated to get underway at 6:00 pm ET from Atlanta.
Related: Why Joe Davis isn't on broadcast for Fox's Dodgers-Braves NLDS Game 3

item.title: [ABC7 Los Angeles] Dodgers land two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in blockbuster deadline deal, sources say
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- For as much as they might have downplayed the possibility behind closed doors, the Los Angeles Dodgers were long seen by rival executives as overwhelming favorites to land generational ace Tarik Skubal. Their farm system was too good, their goals were too lofty, their rotation had become too uncertain. On Saturday night, a day and a half before the trade deadline, they pulled it off. The Dodgers acquired Skubal, the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner, from
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- For as much as they might have downplayed the possibility behind closed doors, the Los Angeles Dodgers were long seen by rival executives as overwhelming favorites to land generational ace Tarik Skubal. Their farm system was too good, their goals were too lofty, their rotation had become too uncertain.
On Saturday night, a day and a half before the trade deadline, they pulled it off.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal, the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner, from the Detroit Tigers for a package of three prospects: outfielder Zhyir Hope, and right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Skubal, a 29-year-old pending free agent, will now headline what was arguably already the best rotation in the sport. Alongside him will be Yoshinobu Yamamoto, making a strong case for a Cy Young of his own, followed by Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani and Tyler Glasnow, all of whom are in varying stages of returning from injury.
The Dodgers had long touted their depth as a reason they didn't necessarily need Skubal. Snell, who has made one start all year, is expected to rejoin the rotation after his next rehab outing. Glasnow, out since May 6 with back spasms, will begin a minor league rehab assignment next week. And though Ohtani is still troubled by a sore left knee that only seems to bother him on the mound, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said earlier this week he fully expects him to pitch in October.
The Game 1 starter, though, will be Skubal, who might be the best pitcher in the world.
Skubal boasts a 2.79 ERA in 16 starts this year, striking out 116 batters and issuing 14 walks in 96 innings. The only thing that could stop him were bone chips that began to cause irritation in his left elbow in late April. Skubal underwent a less-invasive, revolutionary NanoScope procedure and returned in about six weeks. His ERA in July is 2.03. And as he addressed the media in the visiting clubhouse at Sutter Health Park in Sacramento late Saturday night, moments after being informed of the trade, Skubal at one point got choked up.
"Going into the season, this isn't what I planned on doing," Skubal said before getting on the verge of tears while reflecting on his time in Detroit. "But circumstances change, situations change. I'm very appreciative of everything that the Tigers have done for me."
A late bloomer who lasted until the ninth round of the 2018 draft, Skubal began to emerge as one of the game's most talented pitchers in 2022 and 2023 and took it to another level thereafter. From 2024 to 2025, Skubal went 31-10 with a 2.30 ERA and a whopping 469 strikeouts in 387 innings. His 12.6 FanGraphs wins above replacement led all major league pitchers.
When Skubal and members of the Tigers' front office exchanged arbitration figures in the ensuing offseason, the two sides were $13 million apart. An independent arbitrator ruled in favor of Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, rewarding him a $32 million salary as he headed into his free-agent year.
Rumors had swirled throughout the offseason that the Tigers would trade him then. Instead, they doubled down, signing fellow starter Framber Valdez to a three-year, $115 million contract with the hope of winning the AL Central. Instead, the Tigers flopped. By the end of May, they were tied with the Colorado Rockies for the worst record in the majors, prompting executives throughout the industry to assume Skubal would be traded.
The Tigers proceeded to win 28 of their next 46 games, and suddenly it seemed as if Skubal might stay. But their momentum ran out. The Tigers lost back-to-back games to the last-place Kansas City Royals over the weekend and dropped two of three to the Baltimore Orioles thereafter. The last of those losses, on Wednesday night, saw Skubal take the mound and record his 1,000th career strikeout, then sit in the dugout while his team blew a 7-0 lead.
After it was over, the Tigers were seven games below .500, six games out of first place and three games out of a wild-card spot.
To many observing Skubal's availability, it was a death knell to his time in Detroit.
The Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays were all in on Skubal to some extent, with the Brewers, deep in prospects, the favorites among that group. But the Dodgers were the clear frontrunners all along. And now they'll add Skubal to a laundry list of talent they've acquired from the outside over the years, following Ohtani, Snell, Yamamoto, Glasnow, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and, this offseason, Edwin Diaz and Kyle Tucker.
The vast majority of those players came via free agency. The Dodgers loathe the high asking prices at midseason. But in getting Skubal, they parted from an outfield group that is stocked with talent -- one that is still headlined by Josue DePaula, a consensus top-25 prospect, along with Eduardo Quintero, ranked 45th on Kiley McDaniel's latest ESPN rankings. They also maintain all of their young major league starting pitching, namely Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Roki Sasaki.
In Hope and Ryan, though, the Tigers came away with two top-50 prospects.
Hope, 21, was slashing .293/.369/.530 with 23 home runs and 18 stolen bases for the Dodgers' Double-A affiliate and brings explosive power from the left side, top-tier speed and an ability to handle center field.
Ryan, 27, made a brief stint in the major leagues in 2024, putting up a 1.33 ERA in four starts. He then underwent a prolonged rehab from Tommy John surgery and has made eight starts in Triple-A, putting up a 4.46 ERA. He has been out since the middle of June with a hamstring injury, but McDaniel ranked him 49th in his midseason top 50 in May.
Smith, 21, was a third-round pick out of high school in 2023 who has put up a 3.88 ERA in 19 starts at the Class A level this season.
In three months, Skubal will head into the open market with the chance of signing the most lucrative deal ever rewarded to a starting pitcher. Before then, he will join a Dodgers club that boasts the highest run-differential and second-best record in the major leagues -- and help them try to become the first team in NL history to win three consecutive championships.
Asked his thoughts about joining the Dodgers, Skubal took about 15 seconds to compose himself before saying: "Yeah, it's exciting. I'm excited. They've got a good group."

item.content:encoded:
As Shohei Ohtani works his way back to being in top form on the baseball diamond, the star continues to make off-field moves. Through the first two games of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves, Ohtani is hitting .250 with two hits and two strikeouts.
During the Dodgers’ run in the MLB playoffs, New Balance announced that Ohtani’s signature clothing line is now available in select markets.
“Shop the latest styles from the Shohei Ohtani Signature Collection,” New Balance noted in an October 3, Instagram post featuring Ohtani.
“Available now in select markets.”
Additionally, Chandler Bats announced that select fans can purchase a game-model bat designed for Ohtani. These will be a hot commodity as only 1,000 are being released.
“The bat behind the player who changed the game,” Chandler Bats noted in an October 1, Instagram post tagging Ohtani.
“Introducing the SO17.4 Limited Edition — built to @shoheiohtani game-model specifications and crafted by Chandler, available to the world for the first time,” Chandler Bats added.
“Only 1,000 will be made. Sign up to be the first to know at the link in bio.”
Shohei Ohtani’s Contract With Dodgers Includes $68 Million Deferred Annually Starting in 2034
Ohtani signed a massive 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers that is slated to go through the 2033 season. One of the interesting aspects of Ohtani’s deal is that a large portion of the money is deferred.
According to Spotrac, Ohtani will receive $68 million annually from 2034 through 2043. It will be interesting to see what impact this will have on the Dodgers’ potential roster moves during this future time period.
With the way Ohtani’s deal is structured, it allowed the Dodgers to be more aggressive at the MLB trade deadline landing star pitcher Tarik Skubal as one example.
Dodgers Star Shohei Ohtani Is Projected to be MLB’s Top Earner in 2026 at $127 Million
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 25: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walks back to the dugout after striking out against the San Francisco Giants in the top of the eighth inning at Oracle Park on September 25, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)
Ohtani is projected to earn $127 million in 2026, the highest of any baseball player, per Forbes. The star is projected to earn $125 million through endorsements and business ventures compared to $2 million with the Dodgers.
“It’s no wonder that brands are still clamoring for his services, and he recently added a partnership hawking Japanese firm Kirin’s immune health supplements to his long list of sponsors,” Forbes detailed.
“With support like that, Ohtani’s $127 million estimated earnings will exceed the combined totals of the Nos. 2 and 3 players on this year’s Forbes list, with Cody Bellinger and Kyle Tucker set to bank $112.5 million between them.
Injuries have complicated the star’s 2026 campaign, but Ohtani is a rare phenom with the ability to be both an elite hitter and pitcher. This is only going to continue to allow Ohtani’s net worth to grow.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Kiké Hernández’s unusually serious answer to Dodgers’ place in lockout proves players won’t budge
item.dc:creator: Matthew Swigonski
item.description: Despite an injury-plagued season for Shohei Ohtani, 2026 has been a really good year for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
