item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Blake Snell sets the record straight on lil bro dynamic with Tarik Skubal appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Blake Snell has had enough of the confusion. The Dodgers left-hander joined the broadcast booth during Friday's game against the Giants and used the airtime to settle a running clubhouse debate with Tarik Skubal, who has been calling him the younger of the two.
"We got to get this right, you know, it's a lot of comments and people don't know who big bro and little bro is," Snell said in the middle of the game. "I'm big bro. Little bro's right there."
Blake Snell trying to set the record straight on who is big bro and lil bro with Tarik Skubal 🤣🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/SAMX7Vdwg5
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
— Dodgers Nation (@DodgersNation) September 26, 2026
He then turned his attention to the man on the mound. "You never know what he's gonna say," Snell said. "Little bro, he's a crazy guy. But he's throwing cheese right now."
Snell has the math on his side. He turns 34 in December, while Skubal is 29, making the older-brother claim fairly straightforward. That has not stopped Skubal from insisting otherwise.
The dispute went public after the Dodgers clinched the NL West on Sept. 17 with an 8-2 win over the Reds. Amid the celebration, Skubal made his own declaration on camera. "This is my best friend," he said. "He's my little brother."
The two have leaned into the bit hard since Los Angeles acquired Skubal from the Tigers at the trade deadline. They have pulled pranks on each other in the clubhouse, knocked over each other's chairs, and traded Step Brothers-inspired jokes on social media. Skubal recently posted an AI-generated video of the pair rapping Migos' "Hotel Lobby," captioned simply with a reference to his "lil bro."
That post drew attention beyond the joke. Skubal is set to become an unrestricted free agent this offseason, and Dodgers fans have read his comfort in the clubhouse as a sign he may want to stay. He has gone 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA across nine starts since the trade.
Snell, meanwhile, is working his way back after leaving a start against Cincinnati with left groin tightness. Both are expected to anchor a postseason rotation alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto, with Tyler Glasnow also in the mix if health allows.
Whatever the birth order, Los Angeles will take both of them in October.
Related: Dodgers set to receive huge Dalton Rushing boost right before playoffs

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott look like Dodgers’ playoff bullpen anchors
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular. Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning. Tanner Scott in the ninth. Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers. “I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, bu
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular.
Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning.
Tanner Scott in the ninth.
Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers.
“I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, but, yeah, I think it’s just better to have as many guys that you have confidence in leverage (situations),” Roberts said.
Sasaki followed a seven-inning effort by starter Tarik Skubal by striking out two batters in a perfect eighth inning.
Scott retired the side in the ninth to record his 24th save.
On their World Series run last year, the bullpen was something the Dodgers had to work around. They were extremely dependent on their starting pitchers, whom they counted on not only to pitch deeper into games but also make relief contributions. Sasaki’s emergence as closer was as much a reflection of their lack of options as it was of the Japanese fireballer’s gifts.
The Dodgers should enter the playoffs next month with an entirely different feel.
Scott has recovered from his nightmare season last year, looking more like the Padres relief ace who shut down Shohei Ohtani in the 2024 playoffs to earn a $72-million payday with the Dodgers.
As for the 24-year-old Sasaki, he looks even better as a reliever than he did last year.
“I think the fastball’s better,” Roberts said. “I think the split’s better. It’s also nice that he’s already done it. So, just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident. And certainly, the stuff was really good the last couple outings.”
Four of the six fastballs Sasaki threw were clocked at faster than 100 mph.
The other two registered readings of more than 99 mph.
“Overall, he just keeps getting better,” Scott said. “Even when he was starting, I thought he was pretty dominant. For him to get moved to the bullpen as we go into October, it’s huge for us.”
Sasaki started seven games after the All-Star break and was 2-0 with a 3.05 earned-run average. A blister on his pitching hand landed him on the injured list. When he returned earlier this week, he did so as a reliever.
He also struck out two batters in his other relief appearance, a scoreless inning on Tuesday against the San Diego Padres.
“Throughout the season, I’ve sharpened myself technically,” Sasaki said in Japanese. “Compared to last year, I feel much better in that respect.”
Sasaki will likely pitch next in the regular-season finale on Sunday, Roberts said.
He could close out games again in October, as Roberts said there could be games in which he calls on Scott to pitch against a particularly dangerous segment of the opposing lineup earlier in the game.
Scott said he was open to pitching in any situation.
“Just get outs,” Scott said. “That’s all that matters in October. Get outs.
“October is about winning every single game. It really doesn’t matter what roles you get asked to do. Just go out there and do it.”

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers blanquean a los Gigantes con 2 jonrones y 10 ponches de Skubal
SAN FRANCISCO — Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pagés conectaron jonrones en la segunda entrada para respaldar la actuación de Tarik Skubal, quien permitió tres hits en siete innings, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 2-0 a los Gigantes de San Francisco la noche del viernes.
Shohei Ohtani se fue de 4-0 con tres ponches en su tercer juego de regreso tras una estadía de 13 partidos en la lista de lesionados debido a molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Skubal (12-7) ponchó a 10, incluidos cuatro consecutivos durante un tramo, y no otorgó bases por bolas en su décima apertura con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial desde que fue adquirido de Detroit el 2 de agosto. Los Dodgers habían ganado cada una de sus seis salidas anteriores, mientras él tuvo marca de 4-0 en sus últimas cuatro decisiones a lo largo de seis aperturas desde una derrota ante Milwaukee el 16 de agosto.
Fue el cuarto juego de la temporada del ganador vigente en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana con ponches de doble dígito, el segundo con Los Ángeles.
Roki Sasaki lanzó un octavo inning perfecto con un par de ponches antes de que Tanner Scott cerrara el juego, que duró una hora y 53 minutos, para su 24to salvamento. Fue el segundo juego más rápido en los 27 años de historia del estadio.
El abridor de los Gigantes, el dominicano Yunior Marte (0-2), permitió los dos jonrones entre los seis hits que concedió en cinco innings. Más temprano en el día, San Francisco dio la bienvenida de regreso al ex cerrador Camilo Doval, reclamado en waivers después de que lo traspasaran a los Yankees antes de la fecha límite de cambios de 2025. ___

item.title: [FanSided] Why MLB fans should root for Roki Sasaki in the playoffs, not revel in Dodgers downfall
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Crossing the Pacific Ocean and signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers meant cultural and personal transitions for prized Japanese import Roki Sasaki. But when Sasaki officially met the U.S. media in early 2025, he made it clear he and his newest fanbase had two things in common: baseball and grief. item.content:encoded:
Crossing the Pacific Ocean and signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers meant cultural and personal transitions for prized Japanese import Roki Sasaki.
But when Sasaki officially met the U.S. media in early 2025, he made it clear he and his newest fanbase had two things in common: baseball and grief.
Sasaki returned from the injured list this week just as a March 2025 story by the Dodgers’ official website resurfaced on social media. At the time, California was still recovering from the January 2025 wildfires that ravaged the Los Angeles area, an unfortunately familiar sight for their newest pitcher.
Nearly 15 years earlier, Sasaki lost his father, grandparents, and his family’s home in the March 2011 tsunami. He turned to baseball as an escape, just as so many others affected by tragedy often do.
"Los Angeles is facing challenging and difficult times right now,” Sasaki said in January 2025, “and as a member of the Dodgers, starting today, I am dedicated to give my best and strive forward together with the people of the city."
Baseball fans can support Roki Sasaki without rooting for the Los Angeles Dodgers
This might sound contradictory, but hear us out.
We just saw Mets fans overwhelmingly cheer for Pete Alonso, even after he smashed a game-tying home run. Citi Field cared far more about Alonso the player than it did the Orioles as a team. Had the Orioles somehow snuck into the postseason, we imagine there’d be plenty of Mets fans with even the slightest rooting interest.
The same principle — or, at least, an extremely similar one — easily applies to Sasaki. Forget the fact he signed with the reigning World Series champions and played a pivotal role during last year’s title run. He’s still a human being with emotions who went through a horrifically traumatic experience; nearly 20,000 people are believed to have died in the Great East Japan Earthquake, and over 2,550 people remained missing as of 2021.
And above all else, Sasaki hasn’t done anything wrong beyond struggling to hit the strike zone. But compare that to some of the other notable names we’ll see this postseason. San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ramón Laureano each served PED-related suspensions. Boston’s Jarren Duran has feuded with fans and media in a way Red Sox Nation eventually stopped defending.
We’ve long been critical of both Sasaki and how the Dodgers have refused to make him a full-time reliever. Dave Roberts confirmed earlier this week the 24-year-old will pitch out of the bullpen during the postseason, just as he did last October, and the first impressions were positive; Sasaki threw a scoreless inning and didn’t allow a walk against the Padres on Tuesday night.
We wouldn’t blame you for hoping the Dodgers lose in the NLDS. They’re a superteam seeking their third consecutive championship and fourth in six years. At least three players on the active roster — Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, and Mookie Betts — are widely considered locks for the Hall of Fame, and Tarik Skubal is well on his way.
But when Sasaki comes in from the bullpen, try not to be overly hard on him. Save your vitriol for the umpires and broadcasters.

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Dodgers’ Dalton Rushing to get brief audition for postseason spot
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers will activate Dalton Rushing on Friday before their final regular-season series, giving the left-handed power hitter at least a few more days and a handful of at-bats to unleash his swing. The Dodgers are not ruling out a possible spot on a playoff roster, but as of now, they are just focused on giving Rushing the chance to take a few swings in San Francisco in a sign of respect. “At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers will activate Dalton Rushing on Friday before their final regular-season series, giving the left-handed power hitter at least a few more days and a handful of at-bats to unleash his swing.
The Dodgers are not ruling out a possible spot on a playoff roster, but as of now, they are just focused on giving Rushing the chance to take a few swings in San Francisco in a sign of respect.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’
“What he’s done for us this season certainly deserves some (playoff) consideration. That’s kind of giving him the respect and thoughtfulness of what he’s done for us.”
Rushing understands the situation and is fully on board with whatever decision is made.
His season was put in jeopardy when he went on the injured list in early August with an elbow injury that was diagnosed as a small UCL tear with a forearm flexor strain.
Determined to return as both a hitter and a catcher, Rushing worked at both sides of his game and returned on Sept. 1. But the continued throwing work outside of games led to a setback and he went back on the IL less than a week later.
“The at-bat’s really are the only side that I can truly help them in,” Rushing said Thursday. “Even then, it’s just a pinch-hit opportunity and no defense included, so I know that ties their hands up a little bit. But yeah, I’m excited.”
Without much time to make an impact, and the Dodgers also having the option of using left-handed-hitting rookie Josue De Paula on the playoff roster, Rushing is well aware of what he is up against. The club even has the option of using the lefty hitting Hyeseong Kim in the playoffs for his defense and speed.
“No hard feelings on either end,” Rushing said about getting a chance to play in the playoffs. “Obviously you want to play baseball. You feel healthy again to an extent. You feel healthy swinging a bat, so yeah, I want to get back soon.”
The next challenge is determining the extent of his elbow injury. Rushing is swinging pain-free after a platelet-rich plasma injection, but figuring out when he can throw again remains in question.
He is determined to rehab the injury, knowing that some kind of surgical procedure might be needed.
“I think as soon as we get into the offseason, that’s decision time,” Rushing said. “Progressing the way that I’m progressing right now, I’m very optimistic it is going to be totally fine and just think it was a lot of workload increase very quickly. I think that’s what sparked it. Once I got the shot, it felt really, really good.”
Roberts did not say what the full roster move will be on Friday.
VIEW FROM THE TOP
Shohei Ohtani was back in the leadoff spot on Thursday after batting second in his return from the IL on Wednesday.
While his turn as a No. 2 hitter came because the San Diego Padres had left-hander Robbie Ray on the mound, Roberts has not said if batting second against a lefty will be a regular feature of the lineup.
“I’m kind of toying with it clearly,” Roberts said. “But I’m not sure exactly whether he’s going to stick in the one or rotate him depending on the pitcher.”
Ohtani went 1 for 4 with a walk on Wednesday, but the comfort level he showed at the plate pleased Roberts.
“I hope that’s a sign of things to come,” Roberts said. “Taking the first slider from Robbie Ray for a ball, (that) got him into a good count, whereas the last couple weeks he was just hair-on-fire swinging and chasing. It’s a hard way to make a living that way, right? I thought (Wednesday) the patience was really good. I hope that’s more to come.”
CATCHING ON FAST
After starting the first two games of the series against the Padres, catcher Will Smith gave way to backup Hunter Feduccia on Thursday but was available off the bench.
Smith is also set to start two of the three games in San Francisco over the weekend before settling into an everyday role in the playoffs.
In the last five games Smith started, he was batting .421 (8 for 19) with three home runs and five RBIs. Since returning from neck inflammation on Sept. 1, he is batting .255 with four home runs and 11 RBIs in 19 games.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Tarik Skubal, 11-7, 2.85 ERA) at Giants (RHP Yunior Marte, 0-1, 4.66 ERA), Friday, 7:15 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the Los Angeles Dodgers finished their series with the San Diego Padres (at home).
The Dodgers lost by a score of 4-2.
Dodgers Announce Update On 104 MPH Pitcher
The Dodgers have been without one of their pitchers, as Edgardo Henriquez has been out since September 13 with an injury.
During their series with the Padres, they announced the latest update on the two-time World Series Champion.
MLB.com wrote (on September 24): “Has resumed throwing, keeping him as an option to return during the postseason. He’s ineligible to be activated before the end of the regular season.”
Henriquez has gone 4-1 with a 2.85 ERA in 61 games this year.
Looking At Henriquez
Henriquez is in the middle of his third season at the MLB level (all with the Dodgers).
He has gone 6-2 with a 2.73 ERA in 86 career games.
In June, Henriquez turned 24.
Here’s what people have been saying about him this year:
Katie Woo (September 7): “In this story: Edgardo Henríquez threw the third-hardest pitch in MLB this season on Friday (104.5 mph FB). More on the changes he’s made as he becomes a legitimate threat for the October bullpen #Dodgers”
Sarah Langs (September 5): “pitchers to throw 104.0+ mph pitches, pitch-tracking era (2008, incl PS): Aroldis Chapman: 71 Jacob Misiorowski: 23 (2 as RP) Ben Joyce: 14 Jordan Hicks: 13 Jhoan Duran: 9 Mason Miller: 7 Edgardo Henriquez: 2 Ryan Helsley: 2 Mauricio Cabrera: 1 Tyron Guerrero: 1 Camilo Doval: 1 Neftali Feliz: 1″
Fabian Ardaya (September 4): “Tarik Skubal pitched into the sixth, but it remained a grind. Edgardo Henriquez hit 104 mph to strand two baserunners. Skubal’s line: 5.2 IP, 10 H, 2 ER, 1 BB, 6 Ks, 102 pitches, 27% CSW%.”
Los Angeles Dodgers (August 29): “Edgardo with a 104 mph sinker. 🔥”
Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers (who won the National League West) have gone 97-62 in 159 games.
They will visit the San Francisco Giants on Friday.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have punched their ticket to the postseason and will be looking to three-peat.
Last postseason, Yoshinobu Yamamoto had a run for the ages, throwing two complete games, working 28 2/3 innings and closing out the World Series on zero days of rest after throwing six innings the day before. He won World Series MVP and will once again be looking to deliver in October.
Yamamoto was an All-Star once again this year, posting a 2.53 ERA. However, he let Dodgers fans know after his final start of the regular season that he plans to play his best baseball in the postseason.
"Now we're getting into October, so I'd like to live up to the high expectations," Yamamoto said after Wednesday's game.
The Dodgers' postseason rotation this year will feature Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. It's very possible that Yamamoto is not even the Dodgers' No. 2 starter in October. The Dodgers have yet to reveal how they will line up their starters in October, but it's very likely they will have a bye and will have their pick.
If Yamamoto delivers as he did in last year's postseason, the Dodgers will have no problem winning the National League once again.
More MLB: Rays Announce Two-Time All-Star Not Available For ALDS

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres are facing off in the rubber match of their three-game series on Thursday night with plenty at stake for both teams.
The Dodgers, who have already won the National League West division, can clinch a first-round bye with a win or Atlanta Braves loss over the season's final four games.
They're also still chasing the Milwaukee Brewers for the No. 1 seed, but will need some help to secure home-field advantage throughout the postseason.
As for the Padres, they're looking to clinch a postseason spot, with their magic number currently sitting at 1.
Thus, the winner of Thursday's game will be celebrating in some capacity. If it's the Padres, they'll be making a champagne and beer mess in the visitor's clubhouse at Dodger Stadium. If it's the Dodgers, they'll be shaking hands and looking forward to their five-day layoff beginning next week.
Dodgers vs Padres Pitching Matchup on Thursday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the mound for the Dodgers in his final tune-up before the postseason.
Glasnow has been shaky since coming off the injured list at the end of August, sporting a 4.50 ERA over 28 innings with 38 strikeouts to 10 walks. Overall this season, he's 5-1 with a 3.46 ERA and 87 strikeouts across 67.2 innings (12 starts).
Glasnow is expected to be the team's No. 4 starter in the playoffs behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell.
Opposite Glasnow will be Padres right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed nearly five months this season with an elbow injury but has been incredibly sharp since returning.
In his three starts since coming off the IL, Pivetta has allowed just three runs over 14 innings for a 1.93 ERA. He has 11 strikeouts to one walk in that time.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Shohei Ohtani, DH
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Max Muncy, 3B
- Andy Pages, CF
- Hunter Feduccia, C
- Tommy Edman, 2B
How to Watch Dodgers vs Padres on Thursday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Diego Padres on Thursday, Sept. 24 is 7:10 p.m. PT/10:10 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: What Dave Roberts said about Shohei Ohtani's 1st game back from IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani returned to the lineup Wednesday after spending two weeks on the injured list.
Ohtani was activated before Los Angeles' 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres after missing time because of left knee soreness and right biceps discomfort. It was his first game since Sept. 7, and he was inserted into the No. 2 spot against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
The 32-year-old finished 1-for-4 with a walk and two strikeouts. His first at-bat ended with a 99 mph single to right field, and he later hit a 384-foot flyout to center. His biggest missed opportunity came in the fourth inning, when he struck out with the bases loaded during the Dodgers' best scoring chance.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Despite the result, manager Dave Roberts came away encouraged by what he saw from Ohtani.
"He looked good. I thought the at-bat quality was good," said Roberts. "There wasn't any chase. I thought he hit the ball hardest in his first at-bat. It's been a while since he's played in a game, but it just felt like he wasn't sped up at all."
In his final games before landing on the IL, Ohtani had appeared physically compromised at the plate, including moments when he shook out his arm and winced. Los Angeles placed him on the injured list on Sept. 9 after trying to manage the lingering issues while keeping him available.
Ohtani had begun his hitting program about a week before Wednesday's return and had recently faced simulated pitching. He had entered his last game before the IL stint batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs, 89 runs and 80 walks through 134 games.
Roberts said Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Thursday for the series finale. The Dodgers are also still evaluating their batting order against left-handed pitching for the postseason. Against right-handers, Roberts said he would likely put Ohtani back in the leadoff spot and move Mookie Betts to No. 2.
Betts had occupied the leadoff role while Ohtani was away and was batting .366 with six homers, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs in 18 September games.
Ohtani won't take the mound in the playoffs, making his health at the plate all the more important as October approaches.
Related: Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal set to return to Dodgers

The back-up plan was to open with Roki Sasaki, who had missed almost a month due to a blist
item.content:encoded:
With the regular season winding down, the Los Angeles Dodgers have used bullpen days the last two games against the San Diego Padres and San Francisco Giants.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto was originally the probable starter for Tuesday's game against San Diego, but the Dodgers are planning out a schedule to manage Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, while also planning out their playoff rotation.
The back-up plan was to open with Roki Sasaki, who had missed almost a month due to a blister, but the youngster essentially re-wrote the lineup card.
“I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said per Dylan Hernandez of the New York Post. Rather than starting the game, Sasaki was inserted after a one inning each from Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski and Blake Treinen.
The 24-year-old righty pitched a scoreless fourth inning, and struck out two, but did allow two hits in his first outing since August 26th. It was Sasaki's first relief appearance since Game 6 of the World Series last year.
Dodgers' test run with Roki Sasaki was a success
Sasaki is clearly a prideful guy who wants to carve out a career as a starting pitcher. He was not thrilled about the move to the bullpen last season. Unlike many of his teammates, Sasaki isn't signed to a monster contract and likely wants to continue to start games in order to bank a large extension or free agency contract down the road. However, he's clearly in the right state of mind at the moment...perhaps unlike the Dodgers?
It's a little strange that the Dodgers were not planning to deploy Sasaki in relief of this game originally, right? He hadn't come out of the bullpen all season, and baseball players are as routine-oriented as human beings come. It's a little strange, but Sasaki clearly is locked in heading into October.
Sasaki appeared in nine postseason games last year. Sasaki has now appeared in 12 career games as a reliever including both the regular season and postseason, and the Dodgers are 12-0 in those games.
Sasaki has has a 0.66 ERA, 12:5 K:BB, and three saves in just over 13 innings of relief. The hopes are that a rejuvenated and healthy Sasaki can give this shaky, injury-riddled bullpen some stability before a possible three-peat.

item.title: [nbclosangeles.com] Ohtani returns to Dodgers lineup and delivers hit in first at-bat
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort. He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed. “I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.” A roar went up from Dodger fans as
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort.
He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed.
“I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.”
A roar went up from Dodger fans as Ohtani walked to the plate to Michael Bublé's “Feeling Good.” He promptly lined a 2-1 pitch from Ray into right field and the fans got loud again. Ohtani was out at second base when Will Smith grounded into a fielder's choice to third.
Mookie Betts was in Ohtani's usual leadoff spot, where he's been since the two-way superstar went on the injured list on Sept. 8.
Betts is hitting .366 with six home runs, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs scored in 18 games in September. He's tied for third in the major leagues with 26 hits this month, and also ranks among National League leaders this month in extra-base hits, RBIs, total bases, doubles and runs.
Ohtani last played on Sept. 7 against Cincinnati and came in hitting .277 with 30 homers, 80 RBIs, 89 runs scored and 80 walks in 134 games. He appeared physically compromised at the plate, shaking out his arm and wincing at times.
Local
Get Los Angeles's latest local news on crime, entertainment, weather, schools, cost of living and more. Here's your go-to source for today's LA news.
“A few weeks ago you could see that he couldn’t hit a fastball, he was underneath everything and it was a slower swing,” Roberts said. “Just controlling the swing, the barrel, I think that’s something I’ll look at and obviously stuff like the wincing, but I don’t expect to see any of that.”
Roberts said he likely would have Ohtani leading off and Betts hitting second against right-handed pitching.
The Dodgers conclude their three-game set against the Padres on Thursday, then head to San Francisco for three games against the Giants to end the regular season.
Roberts expects to see a focused Ohtani at the plate.
“It’s go-time for all of us and I think he’s in a good spot,” Roberts said. “He's getting ready for the postseason. His mind should be there and my bet is that that’s where it’s at.”
In other moves, pitcher Tarik Skubal was reinstated from the bereavement list. He is scheduled to start Friday at San Francisco. Reliever Kyle Hurt was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Rookie Josue De Paula sent back to minors, could return for postseason
With Ohtani's return, Josue De Paula was sent down to Triple-A to join the Comets in the Pacific Coast League playoffs against the Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula had been in the lineup as the DH.
De Paula quickly became a fan favorite during Ohtani's absence. The 21-year-old New York native reached base safely in 10 of his first 11 games in the majors. He went 2 for 3 with a run scored and a walk while notching his first career triple in the Dodgers' 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday.
“He performed more than admirably,” Roberts said. “This also just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him.”
If De Paula makes the postseason roster, he would serve as a pinch-hitter.
“Josue has been awesome,” said Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations. “Injected some real life and energy into our team.”

item.title: [sandiegouniontribune.com] Padres pregame: Jason Adam activated, Griffin Canning optioned ahead of Game 2 vs. Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Jeff Sanders
item.description: LOS ANGELES — A quad injury cost Jason Adam the chance to help the Padres in last year’s NL Wild Card Series. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — A quad injury cost Jason Adam the chance to help the Padres in last year’s NL Wild Card Series. The team is intent on seeing what the 35-year-old veteran can provide this time around.
Out since late June with a shoulder injury, Adam was activated ahead of Wednesday’s 7:10 p.m. start at Dodger Stadium. To make room, right-hander Griffin Canning was optioned to Triple-A El Paso and reliever Alek Jacob was designated for assignment to allow Adam to rejoin the 40-man roster.
“We saw last year when he got hurt how much we missed him just within the team dynamic and what he provides as experience out there in the bullpen,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “We’ve got a lot more experience than what we had last year in the bullpen right now with those guys being together. But Jason’s a big part of that. He’s a big part of that group out there, and then he’s a pretty darn good pitcher also.”
A first-time All-Star last year, Adam allowed nine runs on seven hits and two walks over 1⅓ innings across three rehab appearances with El Paso. But both he and the team were satisfied with the stuff he showed in hitter-friendly conditions, as well as in live batting practice on Monday, and added his experience to a bullpen that was a strength last year and this year.
Adam’s velocity has trended down from about 95 mph the year the Padres acquired him in 2024 (1.95 ERA) to 94 mph last year (1.93 ERA) to 93 mph this year (2.51 ERA). He missed time earlier in the year as he returned from last year’s season-ending quad surgery and said Tuesday he was eager to get back in the thick of a postseason push.
“Yeah, I’d love to be part of every game,” Adam said after joining the team at Dodger Stadium on Tuesday. “What this team’s doing is really special. So I just want to fill my role, however that looks, and help them win ballgames. We’ve seen pretty well that this team’s good with or without me. I just want to do my part to contribute.”
Ousted from the rotation earlier this summer, Canning was better as a reliever (3.82 ERA in 35⅓ innings) than as a starter (6.79 ERA in 50 ⅓ innings) and had been critical in helping the team piece together games ahead of the trade deadline. But the team only needs three starters for the NL Wild Card Series, he was behind the likes of Robbie Ray, Casey Mize and Randy Vásquez in terms of depth arms for a short series and David Morgan has allowed one run in his last 7⅔ innings to seemingly cement his spot in the depth chart ahead of Canning.
The Padres optioning Canning to the minors means he cannot return to the active roster without an injury until the middle of the NL Division Series, after 15 days.
Jacob, 28, had a 5.58 ERA in 61⅓ innings at Triple-A El Paso and 4.18 ERA in 56 innings across parts of four seasons in the majors. He pitched in three games this year, allowing three runs in five innings as an up-and-down arm.
Ohtani returns, Salas starts
As expected the Dodgers reinstated Shohei Ohtani (biceps, knee from the injured list, as well as left-hander Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list. To make room, outfielder Josue De Paula and Hurt were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ohtani will bat second and serve as the designated hitter for the Dodgers, who have won eight of 11 so far against the Padres this year. Ohtani was 0-for-3 when he last played on Sept. 9 and was in a .122/.295/.184 slide over his last 13 games.
Tonight's #Dodgers lineup vs. Padres: pic.twitter.com/SyL3INJl9z
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 23, 2026
As for the Padres, Ethan Salas will get his first start at Dodger Stadium and second pairing with left-hander Robbie Ray. The only starter he has not worked with is Michael King.
Salas (.627 OPS) was 1-for-2 off the bench on Tuesday. He will bat ninth in a lineup that will see Samad Taylor (.856 OPS) get the start as the DH after Austin Hays did so on Tuesday.
Tonight’s lineup. pic.twitter.com/zLU04b89qh
— San Diego Padres (@Padres) September 23, 2026
While the Padres’ lead on the Diamondbacks was shaved from five to four games with five games left in the season — including three head-to-head matches in San Diego — Tuesday’s loss did little to diminish postseason odds, which are at 93.5% according to FanGraphs.com.
As was the case on Tuesday, any combination of two Padres wins and/or Diamondbacks losses will clinch the team’s third straight postseason berth.
Right-hander Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA) will start at Coors Field for Arizona against Rockies right-hander Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09 ERA). First pitch there is 5:40 p.m..
The Padres, Cubs and Phillies all began Wednesday with identical 87-70 records, although the Padres have to finish ahead of both teams to earn home games in the NL Wild Card Series as they lost both season series.
The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Braves is 1. They are also one game ahead of the Brewers in the race for the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Glass half full
The Dodgers just about emptied the bullpen in Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the Padres. In the aftermath of another bullpen game slowing an offense that ranks first in the majors this month in OPS (.835), a half-glass-full view of what transpired was worth taking forward.
The Padres saw all but two relievers — Kris Bubic and Evan Phillips — in their first shutout loss since Aug. 25 and they still had two more games to wade through in Chavez Ravine.
“They’re really good bullpen arms, so the more you can see them, the better shot you have,” first baseman Ty France said late Tuesday night. “But just move on to (Wednesday) and try to put some better at-bats together.”
The challenge of a bullpen game is a hitter rarely sees a pitcher twice and the Padres are especially proficient when they see relievers more than once.
They rank 10th in the majors with a .712 OPS against relievers, but 17th the first time they see a reliever (.704) and first the second time they see a reliever (.998 OPS).
Right-hander Kyle Hurt was the only pitcher to finish two innings and he allowed just one hit and faced seven batters while taking down the sixth and seventh innings.
Left-hander Jack Dreyer and right-hander Edwin Diaz got through their frames without giving up a baserunner. The rest of the slate of relievers all faced five batters or less.
In short, things went about as optimal as the Dodgers could hope for from a unit ranks 12th in the majors with a 3.82 ERA.
“The Dodgers bullpen’s got some good arms in it,” Stammen said. “They’re bringing out guys that have really good stuff. But the best way to do it is to play a little small ball and try to beat them that way. We just didn’t have the opportunity to play that way and score one run at a time (after) we get down 4-0. That kind of eliminates that way of playing baseball. But you know, we’ve seen their arms now for the rest of the series, and hopefully that benefits us going forward the next two days.”
Wednesday’s pitching matchup
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA)
He’s got a 5.22 ERA in eight starts since the trade deadline. His last start (6 IP, 3 ER) was one of three quality starts as a Padre and a 6-to-2 strikeout-to-walk ratio was his best since the trade. Ray has a 3.81 ERA in 26 career starts against the Dodgers, but he has allowed 15 earned runs in 19 ⅓ runs over four starts over the last two years.
Here is how Ray has fared against current Dodgers:
Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA)
He’s thrown a career-high 179 innings while allowing a career-low 5.7 hits per nine innings. His 14 wins are also a new career best. Yamamoto has a 3.76 ERA in seven regular-season starts against the Padres and a 1.35 ERA in three starts this season (20 (IP, 6 BBs, 22 Ks).
Here is how Yamamoto has fared against current Padres in the regular season:

item.title: [sbsun.com] Shohei Ohtani returns to Dodgers’ lineup – but in a new spot
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday. How refreshed remains to be seen. “These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday.
How refreshed remains to be seen.
“These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start.
“Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. As they are coming back, it’s important for them to feel that way and when you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’ve done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is “considerably” closer to being at his best than he was before going on the IL two weeks ago with biceps and knee issues.
“I would say if he was a ‘5’, he’s probably an ‘8’ or a ‘9’ right now,” Roberts said.
He also returned as a ‘2.’
For the first time since Mookie Betts suffered a fractured hand when he was hit by a pitch on June 16, 2024, Roberts wrote Ohtani’s name in as the No. 2 hitter in the Dodgers’ lineup behind Betts.
Roberts said he plans to go with Betts-Ohtani against left-handed pitching (like the Padres’ Wednesday starter, Robbie Ray) and switch to Ohtani-Betts against right-handed pitching (like Thursday’s starter, Nick Pivetta).
“I just feel good about it,” Roberts said of the decision to use both players at leadoff. “It just makes it tougher to navigate versus left(-handed pitching). There’s a Mookie tax. If you want to get to Freddie (Freeman, batting fourth), there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that and versus a right-hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
In four starts as the leadoff hitter before Ohtani returned, Betts was 8 for 16 with four doubles and two home runs.
Overall, the Dodgers went 10-3 in the 13 games Ohtani missed.
SEE YOU SOON
In order to make room for Ohtani on the active roster, rookie outfielder Josue De Paula was sent to Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he made his Triple-A debut Wednesday night in OKC’s playoff game against Las Vegas.
De Paula is expected to rejoin the Dodgers for next week’s bye week and is still in the running for a spot on the postseason roster. Given a “runway” to get at-bats at DH in Ohtani’s absence, De Paula went 10 for 31 (.323) with five extra-base hits (three doubles, a triple and a home run). Perhaps most impressive, he walked 11 times in 42 plate appearances while striking out just five times.
“It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed,” Roberts said of telling De Paula he was being sent back to the minors – however briefly.
“This was the original thought that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably.”
By sending De Paula out on Wednesday, he will be eligible to be recalled in time for the first game of a best-of-five National League Division Series next week.
“He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said.
Roberts said De Paula showed in his short audition that he is “a special hitter.”
“Doesn’t chase. Moves the ball forward. The threat of power. Lefties don’t faze him,” Roberts recounted. “Hitters don’t (usually) see the ball that quickly out of hand. It’s a gift. No moment is going to be too big for that kid (if he is on the postseason roster).”
PITCHING PLANS
In addition to activating Ohtani on Wednesday, the Dodgers activated starting pitcher Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list and sent right-handed reliever Kyle Hurt back to Triple-A.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Friday night in San Francisco. Blake Snell came out of his bullpen session on Tuesday with no issues in the groin injury that forced him to leave his start last week after one inning. He is expected to start Saturday’s game in San Francisco as a final test before the postseason.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Nick Pivetta, 3-2, 3.30 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 5-1, 3.46 ERA), Thursday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, TBS, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Por BETH HARRIS
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani conectó un hit en su regreso a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles la noche del miércoles, después de perderse dos semanas por molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Bateó segundo como bateador designado contra el abridor zurdo de los Padres de San Diego Robbie Ray.
“No estoy esperando demasiado. Ha pasado un tiempo desde que juega, pero es bueno tenerlo ahí”, comentó el mánager Dave Roberts antes del juego.
Los aficionados ovacionaron a Ohtani cuando caminó hacia el plato con “Feeling Good”, de Michael Bublé. De inmediato conectó una línea al jardín derecho con un lanzamiento de Ray en cuenta de 2-1 y los aficionados volvieron a alborotarse. Ohtani fue puesto out en segunda base cuando Will Smith bateó un rodado para una jugada de selección del fildeador hacia tercera.
Mookie Betts estuvo en el puesto habitual de primer bate de Ohtani, donde ha estado desde que la superestrella ingresó a la lista de lesionados el 8 de septiembre.
Betts batea para .366 con seis jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas, 13 bases por bolas y 18 carreras anotadas en 18 juegos en septiembre. Está empatado en el tercer lugar de las Grandes Ligas con 26 hits este mes, y también figura entre los líderes de la Liga Nacional este mes en hits de extrabase, carreras impulsadas, bases totales, dobles y carreras anotadas.
Ohtani jugó por última vez el 7 de septiembre contra Cincinnati y llegó bateando para .277 con 30 jonrones, 80 carreras impulsadas, 89 carreras anotadas y 80 bases por bolas en 134 juegos. En el plato se le vio físicamente limitado, sacudiendo el brazo y haciendo gestos de dolor en ocasiones.
“Hace unas semanas se podía ver que no podía batear una recta; se quedaba por debajo de todo y el swing era más lento”, señaló Roberts. “Controlar el swing, el punto de contacto, creo que eso es algo en lo que me fijaré y, obviamente, cosas como los gestos de dolor, pero no espero ver nada de eso”.
Los Dodgers concluyen su serie de tres juegos contra los Padres el jueves, y luego viajan a San Francisco para tres juegos contra los Giants para cerrar la temporada regular.
En otros movimientos, el lanzador Tarik Skubal fue reincorporado desde la lista por duelo. Está programado para abrir el viernes en San Francisco. El relevista Kyle Hurt fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
El novato Josue De Paula fue enviado de vuelta a ligas menores; podría regresar para la postemporada
Con el regreso de Ohtani, Josue De Paula bajó a la Triple-A para unirse a los Comets en los playoffs de la Pacific Coast League contra los Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula había estado en la alineación como bateador designado.
De Paula se convirtió rápidamente en un favorito de los aficionados durante la ausencia de Ohtani. El neoyorquino de 21 años se embasó de manera segura en 10 de sus primeros 11 juegos en las Grandes Ligas. Se fue de 3-2 con una carrera anotada y una base por bolas, mientras conseguía el primer triple de su carrera en la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 sobre los Padres el martes.
___

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Wednesday activated Tarik Skubal after the minimum three days on the bereavement list, and optioned Kyle Hurt to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular season start on Friday against the San Francisco Giants on the road at Oracle Park. He was placed on bereavement leave on Sunday, which facilitated Emmet Sheehan making a spot appearance before getting optioned himself on Monday.
In nine starts since joining the Dodgers, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 3.16 xERA with 60 strikeouts and 13 walks in 55 innings.
Hurt was one of eight Dodgers pitchers to combine for a shut out of San Diego in the series opener on Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium, and the only one to pitch multiple innings. Hurt struck out two in his two scoreless frames on Tuesday, allowing only a single.
In 44 games with the Dodgers this season, Hurt has a 4.14 ERA and 3.76 xERA with 58 strikeouts and 23 walks in 45 2/3 innings. The 28-year-old right-hander recorded his first career save on May 27 against the Colorado Rockies in Los Angeles.

item.title: [Yahoo] Shohei Ohtani tiene previsto regresar el miércoles, pero los Dodgers aún tienen dudas por resolver
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo. El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados. "Diría que si
item.content:encoded:
A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo.
El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados.
"Diría que si antes estaba en un nivel de cinco, ahora probablemente esté en un ocho o un nueve", dijo Roberts antes de que ocho lanzadores lideraran la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 contra los Padres de San Diego en el primer partido de la serie.
El martes, los Dodgers redujeron a uno su número mágico para asegurar una exención en la primera ronda. Y antes del partido, recuperaron a otros dos jugadores importantes para la postemporada, al reincorporar del lista de lesionados al jardinero central Andy Pages (fractura en la mano izquierda) y al lanzador derecho Roki Sasaki (ampolla en el dedo medio derecho).
En movimientos correspondientes, los Dodgers enviaron al equipo de Triple A de Oklahoma City al lanzador derecho Emmet Sheehan y al receptor Eliézer Alfonzo.
Sasaki se hizo cargo de la cuarta entrada del partido con relevos y lanzó sin permitir carreras. Permitió un par de sencillos, pero su bola rápida tuvo un poco más de vida en esa breve participación, con un promedio de 98.7 mph y una velocidad máxima de 101.7.
"Pude adaptarme porque ya tenía la experiencia [desde el bullpen] del año pasado", dijo Sasaki a través del intérprete Kensuke Okubo. "Probablemente voy a lanzar en un par de partidos más, así que solo voy a hacer ajustes y seguir avanzando".
Pages se fue de 0 de 2, pero llegó a base dos veces, gracias a un golpeado por lanzamiento y una base por bolas.
"Obviamente, al haber estado fuera un mes, no me siento del todo bien ni tan cómodo al bate", dijo Pages a través del intérprete del equipo, Juan Dorado. "Pero hay cosas [de batear con la máquina Trajekt] que me ayudaron a poder regresar".
Sin embargo, incluso con el regreso de los jugadores, aún hay preguntas que los Dodgers deben responder en la última semana de la temporada:
¿En qué posición bateará Ohtani?
Al menos al principio, Roberts planea colocar a Ohtani al inicio del orden de bateo, como de costumbre. Pero el campocorto Mookie Betts ha entrado en la discusión.
"Sin duda, contra lanzadores diestros [Ohtani] estará ahí", dijo Roberts. "Creo que debería analizar la situación de Mookie contra lanzadores zurdos, pero tengo que pensar en la estructura completa de la alineación".
Ohtani ha sido el primer bateador en todos los partidos que ha sido titular este año. Pero bateó en el segundo lugar en 79 partidos entre las dos temporadas anteriores combinadas.
Incluso sin Ohtani, la alineación de los Dodgers ha estado funcionando bien. El martes, Tommy Edman conectó su segundo jonrón en otros tantos partidos, y Will Smith conectó un jonrón por tercera vez en cuatro días.
¿Está sana la rotación?
El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Blake Snell, quien salió de su apertura la semana pasada por una contractura en la ingle izquierda, realizó una sesión de bullpen el martes. Está programado para una última apertura en la temporada regular el sábado, dijo Roberts.
Eso significa que los cuatro abridores proyectados de los Dodgers para los playoffs están programados para lanzar de este miércoles a sábado, con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tyler Glasnow en el montículo para los dos últimos partidos contra los Padres, y Tarik Skubal y Snell en los dos primeros partidos en San Francisco.
¿Quién es el cerrador?
En resumen, podría cambiar de un día para otro.
"En un mundo perfecto —aunque todos sabemos que el mundo no es perfecto—, me encantaría tener [un cerrador fijo]", dijo Roberts. "Creo que si surge la oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner [Scott] lance una entrada decisiva en la séptima u octava entrada, es difícil dejar pasar esa oportunidad si él es la mejor opción en ese momento. Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se desarrollará la novena entrada.
"Esas son cosas con las que hay que lidiar, y siempre es bueno que la gente las discuta. En este momento no veo a un cerrador que sea solo una persona".
Sasaki asumió ese papel el año pasado. No está claro exactamente cómo lo utilizará Roberts esta vez, pero Roberts dijo que podría ser una opción, dependiendo de cómo lance al regresar de la lista de lesionados.
"El año pasado fue una de esas situaciones de necesidad, dada nuestra situación en cuanto al rendimiento, la salud y la plantilla", dijo Roberts. "Desempeñó ese papel de manera admirable".
El martes, fue uno de los ocho lanzadores de los Dodgers que, en conjunto, lograron una blanqueada en un día de bullpen.
"Hemos tenido mucho talento a lo largo de los años", dijo Roberts. "Pero al sentarnos aquí hoy, al final de la temporada, el bullpen está en la mejor forma en la que ha estado. Eso podría cambiar en un día, en un partido, como todos sabemos. Pero en este momento, me siento muy bien con todos los que están ahí afuera".
El lanzador derecho Edwin Díaz, quien perdió el puesto de cerrador debido a una combinación de lesiones y bajo rendimiento, está en camino de volver a ser considerado para la novena entrada. El martes, retiró a los primeros bateadores de la alineación en orden para una quinta entrada limpia, lo que marcó su tercera salida consecutiva sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
"Si eres uno de los 12 o 13 lanzadores en una posible lista para la postemporada, estás en la lista de los que gozan de confianza", dijo Roberts. "Y él se ha colocado justo en medio de esa conversación. Y considerando todo lo que ha tenido que pasar este año para enderezar el rumbo, es un gran mérito para él".
¿Quién se queda con el último lugar en la banca?
La contienda por ser el bateador zurdo de la banca en la postemporada se ha reducido al novato Josué De Paula y al receptor lesionado Dalton Rushing (distensión en el flexor derecho). Pero con Rushing aún en la lista de lesionados, De Paula parece tener ventaja.
No le des demasiada importancia al movimiento correspondiente de los Dodgers con respecto a Ohtani el miércoles. Si envían a De Paula a las ligas menores a 10 días del primer partido de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, aún puede ser incluido en la plantilla.
Los Dodgers tendrán que hacer otro movimiento en la plantilla más adelante en la semana, cuando planean activar a Rushing. Si envían a un jugador a las ligas menores para hacerle espacio a Rushing, ese jugador solo sería elegible para el inicio de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional como transacción correspondiente a un movimiento a la lista de lesionados.

item.title: [mlb.com] The teams no one wants to play in October
item.dc:creator: Travis Sawchik
item.description: The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same. The regular season and the postseason reward different things. Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. A team can survive a thin rotation, a shaky middle-relief corps or a few light-hitting positions for a while – but it's much harder to hide those weaknesses over six months. October is different. The games are fewer, off-days greater.
item.content:encoded:
The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same.
The regular season and the postseason reward different things.
Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. A team can survive a thin rotation, a shaky middle-relief corps or a few light-hitting positions for a while – but it's much harder to hide those weaknesses over six months.
October is different.
The games are fewer, off-days greater. The urgency is heightened. Teams concentrate work among their best pitchers and lineups. Managers can shorten games with their best relievers. And one superstar hitter or ace can have an outsized influence on a short series.
Variance matters, too. A cleanup hitter can go 2-for-20 in April and the season keeps moving. Go 2-for-20 in October and the season might be over.
“Scary” is not necessarily the same as “best.” It is about concentration of talent, the ability to hide weaknesses, who is peaking at the right time, and the number of ways a team can make a short series tilt quickly.
I started with a simple framework: Which teams can shorten a series with two or three dominant starters? Which have a bullpen capable of essentially ending a game after five or six innings? Which lineups have enough power to avoid having to string together three or four hits against elite pitching? Which teams have deeper lineups to grind down opponents?
Who are the teams nobody wants to see in October?
The concentrated dynamo: the Dodgers
The Dodgers are the obvious answer.
Yes, they have some health question marks with Blake Snell and Shohei Ohtani. Yes, Edwin Díaz has not been the end-game piece they were hoping for in the bullpen. And, yes, their overall team slugging is down double-digit points from each of the last two years as well. But they are still a heavy World Series favorite no one wants to play.
A rotation led by Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow is as good as it gets, and they are backed by a lineup that, while aging, still ranks as one of the best in the game. The market and models still believe they are the team to beat; FanGraphs gives them a 29.3% chance to win the title.
The team without a weakness: Brewers
While the Dodgers are the favorites, there's a case to be made that the Brewers are the scarier October opponent.
And after struggling out of the gate, Milwaukee is 82-44 since May 1 – five games better than the Rays, the next-ranking team. They've been above average in every month since April.
The terrifying thing about the Brewers is that there isn't an obvious way to attack them.
They have the most dominant pitcher in the game this year in Jacob Misiorowski, who unlike in his rookie year has shown no signs of slowing down. Misiorowski remains dominant in the second half with a 29% K-BB mark. His elevated velocity has held steady. And nearly as unhittable in the second half is Logan Henderson, who sports a 2.22 ERA, is holding opponents to a .171 average, and enjoys a 26.9 K-BB% mark since the All-Star break.
Getting the starter out doesn't make life easier either. The Brewers' reliever corps ranks fourth in ERA (3.41) and third in fWAR (6.6) out of all 30 teams.
Supporting those arms is an excellent defense.
And while the Brewers lack elite power, they string together quality at-bats with seven qualified Brewers hitters having an OPS+ of 100 or better, trailing only the Dodgers (eight) in the projected postseason field. The Phillies, by contrast, have two.
They are also trending the right way. The Brewers are 17-9 over the 30 days, tied for the second-best mark in baseball.
FanGraphs gives the Brewers the second-best title chances after the Dodgers (13.9%). They are a team built for the regular season and October.
OK, those are obvious contenders. What about other clubs?
The middling (potential) division winner: Guardians
The Guardians were one of the teams that actually won the Trade Deadline. Those added reinforcements, along with some positive regression from first-half slumpers like Steven Kwan, picked up a sluggish offense. They rank eighth in the Majors in runs since Aug. 1 (216 entering Tuesday).
A less obvious October advantage? Cleveland leads baseball in the percentage of plate appearances in which it enjoys the platoon advantage, at 77%, compared with a league average of 58.3%. In a five-game or seven-game series against a manager trying to optimize every matchup, that can become consequential.
And what really makes this team dangerous is the pitching staff.
The Guardians are one of three teams projected to be in the field that roster two pitchers that rank in the top 10 of fWAR in the second half of the season (the Dodgers are another, along with the Phillies).
Gavin Williams and Parker Messick have emerged as front-line starters this year. Tanner Bibee is a strong No. 3. While middle relief has hurt the club all season, being able to move a starter to the relief group should build a better bridge to closer Cade Smith.
Most teams that spend much of a season hovering around .500 don't have this kind of top-end pitching.
The Guardians are also hot, tied for the second-best record (17-9) in the Majors over the last month – tied with the Dodgers, Brewers, Braves and Padres – entering play Tuesday. Only the Rays (19-8) are better – but the Rays don't quite have the Guardians’ top-end starting pitching depth.
As the playoff picture stands entering Tuesday, the Guardians would face the winner of the White Sox (+42 run differential) or Rangers (-34 run differential) in the ALDS, with AL East clubs competing on the other side of the bracket. That's an extremely favorable path for a team with sneaky upside.
The unusual build: Cubs 
The Cubs are perhaps the strangest team on this list because their postseason case is built around the idea that an elite lineup and defense can overwhelm the quality and concentration of October pitching.
In the second half they've posted a 125 wRC+, 25% better than league average, and they've combined for a 134 wRC+ over the last month. That's an incredible number.
The 2018 Dodgers are an interesting comp. They led the NL with a 111 wRC+, including a 134 mark over the last 30 days of the season – just like these surging Cubs. They were also an elite defensive team lacking an elite rotation.
Those Dodgers won a relatively modest 92 games in the regular season but advanced to the World Series. Perhaps the Cubs can, too. While an ace makes life easier, there are different paths through October.
The wild card among wild cards: Padres
If you believe in timing and momentum, believe in the Padres.
For much of the season they have been a confounding team, much like their face of the franchise, Fernando Tatis Jr.
Over the last month, the Padres are third in baseball with a 118 wRC+.
Moreover, the pitching has become more interesting – deeper and healthier – at exactly the right time.
Nick Pivetta returned from his long absence to post a 1.93 ERA over three September starts.
Michael King has outperformed peripherals to become a 12-game winner with a 3.03 ERA. Robbie Ray, acquired at the Trade Deadline, gives them another veteran option.
They also have one great postseason advantage: If they can hand a lead over to the bullpen it's lights out with Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller closing out games.
The Padres own the end game, and at no time does that matter more than in October.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Sidelined last year, Evan Phillips & Brock Stewart are ready for October
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Last year at this time, Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart were both recovering from surgeries and unavailable to pitch. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Last year at this time, Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart were both recovering from surgeries and unavailable to pitch. They were around the team but unable to contribute during the stretch run and postseason. This year, both veteran right-handers are two key cogs in an increasingly deep Dodgers bullpen and an important part of their October puzzle.
Phillips had Tommy John surgery in June 2025, wiping out the last half of last season and the first half of this one. When he returned from the injured list in July, the Dodgers were cautious in his usage, not using him on back-to-back days for his first four weeks, and used him on one day rest only four times during that stretch.
The results were spotty at first, allowing runs in five of his first seven appearances, including an uncharacteristic four home runs in such a short span. Since then, Phillips has allowed runs in only three of his last 21 appearances, and the lone home run surrendered was last Monday to Elly De La Cruz, which seems to be a rite of passage for everybody these days.
“Evan as you would expect, the first handful of outings were inconsistent coming off Tommy John, but I’d say the last [few] have been kind of who he is, and it’s been fun to see,” manager Dave Roberts said recently. “There’s a two-seamer, there’s a four-seamer, and some sweepers getting some awkward swings, some chase. That’s been good, and his command has been a lot better, too.”
Phillips in his 28 games has 28 strikeouts against only three unintentional walks. Since the start of August, the Dodgers have used Phillips more aggressively, pitching on back-to-back days five times, and he pitched three times in four days in three different stretches, and during that span has a 2.30 ERA and 2.46 FIP.
“I appreciate what they’ve done, trying to build me up, plus also protect me, plus giving me advantageous lanes while also challenging me,” Phillips said. “It’s been great so far, and I definitely feel like I’m coming closer and closer to that best version of myself that I have been and continue to strive to be.”
Stewart, a sixth-round draft pick of the Dodgers in 2014, was reacquired by the team at the 2025 trade deadline, but he pitched in only four games for them before succumbing to right shoulder debridement surgery in September. This year the right-hander has a 2.45 ERA and 2.53 xERA in his 27 games, with 24 strikeouts and seven unintentional walks in 25 2/3 innings, including a scoreless first inning to start Tuesday night’s bullpen-game shutout of the San Diego Padres.
“When Brock’s healthy, he’s as good as anyone we have,” Roberts said Tuesday. “For us, it’s just trying to manage him the right way and keep him strong and healthy. He’s been great.”
“That’s very cool to hear. I just go out there and throw it, that’s literally all I focus on. But people tell me that my — you know, I throw five pitches, which helps as a reliever,” Stewart said. “They tell me my stuff is pretty good, and it’s always nice to hear that. But I don’t know, I just go out there and throw it, try to compete as best I can, and hope it works out.
Roberts wasn’t wrong. Since returning to the majors in 2023 with the Minnesota Twins, Stewart has a 2.45 ERA and 2.78 xERA, which ranks 10th and ninth, respectively, among the 576 major league pitchers with at least 100 innings over the last four years. Tarik Skubal, with two Cy Young Awards during that stretch, has a 2.50 ERA and 2.73 xERA, for example.
But staying on the field has been a problem for Stewart, who this season alone has been on the injured list three different times — recovering from shoulder surgery, bone spur in his left foot, and shoulder discomfort — inactive for a total of 95 games. Since 2023, Stewart has also been on the injured list with elbow soreness, shoulder tendinitis, a shoulder strain, a hamstring strain, and shoulder inflammation, limited to just 106 2/3 total innings over the last four seasons.
“I feel good, but I’ve told everybody though, one day at a time. I’ve been hurt a lot so I always try to take things one day at a time. But I’m happy with the way I feel, happy with the way I felt today,” Stewart said. “Getting close to the finish line, but happy with how I feel, happy with how the stuff is coming out. I feel like I’m in a good spot and can hopefully help out.”
Stewart has pitched in the postseason only once, in three games over two series with the Minnesota Twins in 2023. Phillips was an October stalwart for the Dodgers since he was acquired on a waiver claim in 2021. In 12 appearances for the Dodgers in the playoffs, Phillips has yet to allow a run, over 15 1/3 innings, with 21 strikeouts and six unintentional walks. Phillips missed out on the World Series in 2024 with a right rotator cuff injury suffered during the NLCS, and was sidelined for all of last October.
“I love pitching in the postseason, I love competing with these guys. In 2024, missing out on the World Series, but I tried to dig in on the fact that I helped us get there, and played quite a large part in the Division Series and Championship Series. Obviously I want to see it all to the end, and help us carry that trophy off the field,” Philips said. “I’m just as eager as ever. Fortunate that I feel healthy at this time, and just trying to build on that, continue to chip away, and be the best I can when it matters most.”
This season, only Tanner Scott, Edwin Díaz, and Alex Vesia have a higher average-leverage index than Phillips and Stewart among Dodgers relievers. Phillips and Stewart have each saved a game this year, and Phillips has done so in the past with 46 saves with the Dodgers. Roberts said he’d feel comfortable with either Phillips or Stewart getting a save opportunity in October, along with a group that includes Tanner Scott and the just-activated Roki Sasaki.
“This year, more than any other year, I think there’s more guys we feel comfortable closing out games,” Roberts said.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki ditches Dodgers plan with striking U-turn in prep for 3-peat quest
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The initial plan called for Roki Sasaki to pitch an inning or two as an opener. Sasaki had other ideas. “I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said in Japanese. Because Sasaki will be deployed as a reliever in the playoffs, he figured he should spend the remainder of the regular season becoming reacquainted with the role. item.content:encoded:
The initial plan called for Roki Sasaki to pitch an inning or two as an opener.
Sasaki had other ideas.
“I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said in Japanese.
Because Sasaki will be deployed as a reliever in the playoffs, he figured he should spend the remainder of the regular season becoming reacquainted with the role.
So instead of throwing the first and second innings of the Dodgers’ 7-0 victory over the San Diego Padres on Tuesday night, Sasaki pitched the fourth.
Returning from a month-long stay on the injured list, Sasaki pitched in relief for the first time this season.
What was most memorable about his night wasn’t that he struck out two batters or threw six of his 20 pitches faster than 99 mph. Rather, what was most striking was his embrace of his move out of the Dodgers’ rotation.
Sasaki was reluctant to make the switch last year, doing so only as a last-ditch effort to salvage an otherwise disastrous rookie season. The decision made him an October hero, as the team’s lack of options made him the closer almost by default.
He returned to the rotation this year and was 5-5 with a 4.56 earned-run average through his first 23 games, all of them starts. His form improved over the course of the season, and he was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break. But in the last of those starts, which was on Aug. 26 in Atlanta, he developed a blister on the middle finger of his pitching hand.
Starting games was a source of pride for Sasaki. When he agreed to try pitching in relief last year, he made the Dodgers promise him they would use him as a starter this season.
Sasaki didn’t require as much convincing when team officials started talking to him about a role change on the Dodgers’ recent trip to Cincinnati.
The Dodgers will use a four-man rotation in the playoffs, and they have four Cy Young Award-caliber pitchers in Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Sasaki could do the math. If he was going to pitch in the postseason, it would be as a reliever.
“I think it’s important to make the roster,” Sasaki said.
Something else: The Dodgers kept their word about him starting games, and Sasaki wanted to repay them.
“In the first half of the season, they used me as a starter even when I wasn’t pitching well,” he said.
Sasaki didn’t pitch more than five innings in any of his first five starts. His ERA at that point was 6.35. His fastball velocity was down and his command was non-existent.
The Dodgers would have been justified in removing him from the rotation.
They didn’t.
They could have sent him to the minor leagues.
They didn’t.
That meant something to Sasaki.
“This time,” Sasaki said, “I want to be able to contribute to the team in whatever shape.”
The feelings point to a growing trust that has developed between Sasaki and the Dodgers.
At this stage of the season last year, they didn’t seem to be on the same page. As he shined as their closer last October, Dodgers officials and coaches told stories about how they helped Sasaki rediscover his 100-mph fastball. Sasaki downplayed the team’s role in his resurgence, saying he figured out what he was doing wrong by watching videos of himself pitching in high school.
Sasaki is said to have become more open to instruction this season, which contributed to an improved fastball as well as the incorporation of a different variation of his signature forkball.
He is also physically stronger than he did last year. Fatigue was a factor for him in the postseason, and by the World Series, he looked like a spent cartridge. To close out Game 7 of the World Series, manager Dave Roberts went to Yamamoto, who was pitching his third inning in relief a day after making a six-inning start.
Sasaki looks more capable of shouldering a reliever’s schedule and workload.
Sasaki closing games in the upcoming postseason is “certainly an option,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Edwin Diaz has worked his way back into ninth-inning consideration by posting three consecutive scoreless appearances since his return from his latest IL stint. Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer this season, but Roberts said there could be instances in which the left-hander is used earlier in games in high-leverage situations.
Sasaki said he would pitch whenever asked.
That could be determined by how he looks over this final week of the regular season. Roberts said he will likely pitch next on Friday in San Francisco.
This time around, there isn’t any hesitation on the part of Sasaki. This time around, he really wants to do this.

item.title: [Just Baseball] The Dodgers' Max Muncy Continues To Be Underrated | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Clay Snowden
item.description: Los Angeles, California. The city of movie stars, names and big personalities. Oh yeah, and championships, with the two most recent going to the Dodgers.
